akhfash:3-3.t: And He said ﴿إِنَّا هَدَيْنَاهُ ٱلسَّبِيلَ إِمَّا شَاكِراً وَإِمَّا كَفُوراً ﴾; likewise ﴿إِمَّا ٱلعَذَابَ وَإِمَّا ٱلسَّاعَةَ﴾: it is as if you had not mentioned "إمَّا" ("either"); and if you wish, you begin afresh with what follows it and make it nominative.

akhfash:6-6.t: And He said ﴿عَيْناً يَشْرَبُ بِهَا عِبَادُ ٱللَّهِ﴾: He made it accusative in three ways. If you wish, it is on His words ﴿يَشْرَبُونَ﴾ [5] "﴿عَيْناً﴾" ("they drink … a spring"); if you wish, on ﴿يَشْرَبُونَ مِن كَأْسٍ كَانَ مِزَاجُهَا كَافُوراً﴾ ﴿عَيْناً﴾; and if you wish, by way of praise (madḥ), as when a man mentions someone to you and you say "العاقلَ واللبيبَ" ("the intelligent one, the discerning one!"), that is: you have mentioned the intelligent, discerning one — on the pattern "أَعْنِي عَيْناً" ("I mean a spring").

akhfash:9-9.t: [And He said] ﴿وَلاَ شُكُوراً﴾: if you wish, you make it the plural of "الشُكْر" (thanks), and make "الكُفُور" the plural of "الكُفْر" (ingratitude), like "الفَلْس" and "الفُلُوس". And if you wish, you make it a single maṣdar (verbal noun) with a plural meaning, like "قَعَد قُعُودا" and "خَرَج خُروجا".

akhfash:13-14.t: And He said ﴿مُّتَّكِئِينَ﴾: by way of praise (madḥ), or on "جَزَاهُمْ جَنَّةً مَتُكَّئِيِنَ فيها" ("He rewarded them with a garden, reclining in it") as a ḥāl (circumstantial). And you may say "جَزاَهُم ذلكَ قِياماً" ("He rewarded them with that, standing"). Likewise ﴿وَدَانِيَةً﴾ is a ḥāl or by way of praise; its accusative is only due to an implied verb. It is also permissible in His words ﴿وَدَانِيَةً﴾ for it to be on two aspects: on "وجزاهمْ دانيةً ظِلاَلُها" ("and He rewarded them with [a garden] whose shades are near"), as you say "اَعطَيْتُكَ جَيْداً طَرَفاهُ" ("I gave you one whose two ends are good") and "رأينَا حَسَناً وَجْهُهُ" ("we saw one whose face is handsome"). «[Translator's note: only one of the "two aspects" is spelled out in the source.]»

akhfash:17-17.t:
And He said ﴿كَانَ مِزَاجُهَا زَنجَبِيلاً﴾: He made "the spring" (العين) accusative in four ways: on "يُسْقَوْنَ عَيْناً" ("they are given a spring to drink"), or as a ḥāl (circumstantial), or as a badal (substitute) for "the cup", or by way of praise (madḥ), the verb being implied. Some said that "سلسبيل" is a description (ṣifa) of the spring, describing it as «سَلْسَبِيل». And some said: "He only meant 'a spring that is named «سَلْسَبِيل»' (عَيْناً تُسَمَّى سَلْسَبِيلاً)", that is: it is so called because of its excellence, that is: it is described (thus) to people, just as you say "الأعوجيّ" and "الأَرْحَبِيّ" and "المَهْرِيّ من الإِبل" (the Mahrī among camels); and just as horses, when described, are attributed to these well-known, pedigreed horses, so likewise the spring is attributed by being named [«سَلْسَبِيل»], because the Qur'an points to the speech of the Arabs. The poet said — and Yūnus recited it to us thus — [in the kāmil metre; this is the two hundred and seventy-fourth verse cited as evidence]:
صَفْراءُ مِنْ نَبْعٍ يُسَمَّى سَهْمُها * مِنْ طُولِ ما صَرَعَ الصُّيُودَ الصَّيِّبُ
(A yellow [bow] of nabʿ wood, whose arrow is called — from how long it has felled the game — "the sure-hitter".)
He put "الصيِّب" in the nominative because he did not mean "its arrow is named 'the sure-hitter'" (يسمى سهمها بالصيِّب); rather "الصيِّب" is a description of the name and of the arrow. And his words "يسمى سهمها" mean: its arrow is spoken of. And some said: "No, rather it is the name of the spring, and it is definite; but since it is the end of a verse [and] it had fatḥa, you added the alif to it, as with ﴿قَوَارِيرَاْ﴾."

akhfash:20-20.t: And He said ﴿وَإِذَا رَأَيْتَ ثَمَّ رَأَيْتَ نَعِيماً﴾: He means to make "رأَيْتَ" not take an object (intransitive), as one says "ظننت في الدار خيرٌ" ("I supposed: in the house there is good") on account of the place of his supposing; and He reported the place of his seeing.

celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿هَلْ﴾ indeed (qad) ﴿أَتَى عَلَى الْإِنْسَانِ﴾ Adam ﴿حِينٌ مِنَ الدَّهْرِ﴾ forty years ﴿لَمْ يَكُنْ﴾ in it ﴿شَيْئًا مَذْكُورًا﴾ in it he was a form of clay that was not mentioned; or what is meant by "the human being" is the species, and by "the period" the duration of pregnancy.

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿إِنَّا خَلَقْنَا الْإِنْسَانَ﴾ the species ﴿مِنْ نُطْفَةٍ أَمْشَاجٍ﴾ mixtures, i.e. from the fluid of the man and the fluid of the woman, mixed and blended; ﴿نَبْتَلِيهِ﴾ We test him with legal obligation; the clause is resumptive, or an anticipated ḥāl (circumstantial, ḥāl muqaddara), i.e. intending to test him when he becomes fit for it; ﴿فَجَعَلْنَاهُ﴾ because of that ﴿سَمِيعًا بَصِيرًا﴾

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿إِنَّا هَدَيْنَاهُ السَّبِيلَ﴾ We made clear to him the path of guidance by sending messengers, ﴿إِمَّا شَاكِرًا﴾ i.e. a believer ﴿وَإِمَّا كَفُورًا﴾ two ḥāls (circumstantials) from the object, i.e. We made [it] clear to him in his anticipated state of gratitude or of unbelief; إِمَّا is for detailing the states.

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿إِنَّا أَعْتَدْنَا﴾ We have prepared ﴿لِلْكَافِرِينَ سَلَاسِلَ﴾ by which they are dragged in the Fire ﴿وَأَغْلَالًا﴾ on their necks, to which the chains are fastened, ﴿وَسَعِيرًا﴾ a fire kindled, i.e. stirred up, with which they are punished.

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿إِنَّ الْأَبْرَارَ﴾ plural of بَرّ or بَارّ, and they are the obedient, ﴿يَشْرَبُونَ مِنْ كَأْسٍ﴾ it is a vessel for drinking wine while the wine is in it, and what is meant is: of wine, naming the contents by the name of the container; مِنْ is partitive; ﴿كَانَ مِزَاجُهَا﴾ what it is mixed with ﴿كَافُورًا﴾

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿عَيْنًا﴾ a badal (substitute) for كَافُورًا, having its scent; ﴿يَشْرَبُ بِهَا﴾ from it ﴿عِبَادُ اللَّهِ﴾ His friends, ﴿يُفَجِّرُونَهَا تَفْجِيرًا﴾ they lead it wherever they wish from their dwellings.

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿يُوفُونَ بِالنَّذْرِ﴾ in obedience to Allah ﴿وَيَخَافُونَ يَوْمًا كَانَ شَرُّهُ مُسْتَطِيرًا﴾ widespread,

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿وَيُطْعِمُونَ الطَّعَامَ عَلَى حُبِّهِ﴾ i.e. of the food, and their desire for it, ﴿مِسْكِينًا﴾ a poor person ﴿وَيَتِيمًا﴾ who has no father ﴿وَأَسِيرًا﴾ meaning one imprisoned by right,

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿إِنَّمَا نُطْعِمُكُمْ لِوَجْهِ اللَّهِ﴾ seeking His reward; ﴿لَا نُرِيدُ مِنْكُمْ جَزَاءً وَلَا شُكُورًا﴾ thanks; in it is the reason for the feeding. Whether they actually said that, or Allah knew it of them and praised them for it, there are two views.

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿إِنَّا نَخَافُ مِنْ رَبِّنَا يَوْمًا عَبُوسًا﴾ in which faces grimace, i.e. of hateful aspect because of its severity, ﴿قَمْطَرِيرًا﴾ severe in that.

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿فَوَقَاهُمُ اللَّهُ شَرَّ ذَلِكَ الْيَوْمِ وَلَقَّاهُمْ﴾ gave them ﴿نَضْرَةً﴾ beauty and radiance in their faces ﴿وَسُرُورًا﴾

celaleyn:12-12.t: ﴿وَجَزَاهُمْ بِمَا صَبَرُوا﴾ for their patience in refraining from disobedience ﴿جَنَّةً﴾ which they were made to enter ﴿وَحَرِيرًا﴾ which they were clothed in,

celaleyn:13-13.t: ﴿مُتَّكِئِينَ﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the implied nominative [pronoun] of أُدْخِلُوهَا ﴿فِيهَا عَلَى الْأَرَائِكِ﴾ couches in canopied alcoves; ﴿لَا يَرَوْنَ﴾ they do not find — a second ḥāl — ﴿فِيهَا شَمْسًا وَلَا زَمْهَرِيرًا﴾ i.e. neither heat nor cold; it is also said that al-zamharīr is the moon, so it is radiant without sun or moon.

celaleyn:14-14.t: ﴿وَدَانِيَةً﴾ near; conjoined to the position (maḥall) of لَا يَرَوْنَ, i.e. not seeing; ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ from them ﴿ظِلَالُهَا﴾ its trees, ﴿وَذُلِّلَتْ قُطُوفُهَا تَذْلِيلًا﴾ its fruits brought low, so that the one standing, the one sitting and the one lying down can reach them.

celaleyn:15-15.t: ﴿وَيُطَافُ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ in it ﴿بِآنِيَةٍ مِنْ فِضَّةٍ وَأَكْوَابٍ﴾ cups without handles ﴿كَانَتْ قَوَارِيرَا﴾

celaleyn:16-16.t: ﴿قَوَارِيرَ مِنْ فِضَّةٍ﴾ i.e. they are of silver, whose inside can be seen from the outside, like glass; ﴿قَدَّرُوهَا﴾ i.e. those who go round ﴿تَقْدِيرًا﴾ according to the measure of the drinkers' thirst, without more or less, and that is the most delightful drink.

celaleyn:17-17.t: ﴿وَيُسْقَوْنَ فِيهَا كَأْسًا﴾ i.e. wine ﴿كَانَ مِزَاجُهَا﴾ what it is mixed with ﴿زَنْجَبِيلًا﴾

celaleyn:18-18.t: ﴿عَيْنًا﴾ a badal (substitute) for زَنْجَبِيلًا ﴿فِيهَا تُسَمَّى سَلْسَبِيلًا﴾ meaning that its water is like the ginger in which the Arabs delight, easy to swallow in the throat.

celaleyn:19-19.t: ﴿وَيَطُوفُ عَلَيْهِمْ وِلْدَانٌ مُخَلَّدُونَ﴾ in the form of youths, not growing grey; ﴿إِذَا رَأَيْتَهُمْ حَسِبْتَهُمْ﴾ because of their beauty and their spreading out in service ﴿لُؤْلُؤًا مَنْثُورًا﴾ from its string or from its shell, and it is more beautiful than it is otherwise.

celaleyn:20-20.t: ﴿وَإِذَا رَأَيْتَ ثَمَّ﴾ i.e. if seeing occurs on your part in Paradise, ﴿رَأَيْتَ﴾ the answer (jawāb) of إِذَا ﴿نَعِيمًا﴾ indescribable ﴿وَمُلْكًا كَبِيرًا﴾ vast, without limit.

celaleyn:21-21.t: ﴿عَالِيَهُمْ﴾ above them; so it is accusative as an adverb (ẓarf), and it is the khabar (predicate) of a mubtadaʾ (subject) after it; in one reading, with sukūn on the yāʾ, it is the mubtadaʾ and what follows it is the khabar; the pronoun attached to it refers to those conjoined to them; ﴿ثِيَابُ سُنْدُسٍ﴾ silk, ﴿خُضْرٌ﴾ in the nominative, ﴿وَإِسْتَبْرَقٌ﴾ in the genitive: the thick kind of brocade, which is the linings, while the sundus is the outer faces; in one reading the reverse of what was mentioned for the two; in another [خُضْرٌ وَإِسْتَبْرَقٌ] both in the nominative, and in another both in the genitive. [Translator's note: the printed text shows إِسْتَبْرَقٌ with nominative tanwīn while the gloss says "in the genitive"; translated as written.] ﴿وَحُلُّوا أَسَاوِرَ مِنْ فِضَّةٍ﴾ and in another place "of gold", to indicate that they are adorned with both kinds, together and separately; ﴿وَسَقَاهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ شَرَابًا طَهُورًا﴾ intensive, for its purity and cleanness, unlike the wine of this world.

celaleyn:22-22.t: ﴿إِنَّ هَذَا﴾ bliss ﴿كَانَ لَكُمْ جَزَاءً وَكَانَ سَعْيُكُمْ مَشْكُورًا﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no further explanation here]

celaleyn:23-23.t: ﴿إِنَّا نَحْنُ﴾ an emphasis (tawkīd) of the noun of إِنَّ, or a separating pronoun (faṣl); ﴿نَزَّلْنَا عَلَيْكَ الْقُرْآنَ تَنْزِيلًا﴾ the khabar (predicate) of إِنَّ; i.e. We sent it down in portions and did not send it down all at once.

celaleyn:24-24.t: ﴿فَاصْبِرْ لِحُكْمِ رَبِّكَ﴾ upon you, to convey His message, ﴿وَلَا تُطِعْ مِنْهُمْ﴾ i.e. the unbelievers ﴿آثِمًا أَوْ كَفُورًا﴾ i.e. ʿUtba ibn Rabīʿa and al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra, who said to the Prophet ﷺ: "Give up this matter." It may also be that every sinner and unbeliever is meant, i.e. do not obey either of them, whoever he is, in the sin or unbelief he calls you to.

celaleyn:25-25.t: ﴿وَاذْكُرِ اسْمَ رَبِّكَ﴾ in prayer ﴿بُكْرَةً وَأَصِيلًا﴾ meaning the dawn, noon and afternoon prayers,

celaleyn:26-26.t: ﴿وَمِنَ اللَّيْلِ فَاسْجُدْ لَهُ﴾ meaning the sunset and night prayers ﴿وَسَبِّحْهُ لَيْلًا طَوِيلًا﴾ pray voluntary prayer in it, as preceded: two-thirds of it, or half, or a third.

celaleyn:27-27.t: ﴿إِنَّ هَؤُلَاءِ يُحِبُّونَ الْعَاجِلَةَ﴾ this world ﴿وَيَذَرُونَ وَرَاءَهُمْ يَوْمًا ثَقِيلًا﴾ severe, i.e. the Day of Resurrection; they do not work for it.

celaleyn:28-28.t: ﴿نَحْنُ خَلَقْنَاهُمْ وَشَدَدْنَا﴾ strengthened ﴿أَسْرَهُمْ﴾ their limbs and joints, ﴿وَإِذَا شِئْنَا بَدَّلْنَا﴾ We would make ﴿أَمْثَالَهُمْ﴾ in form, in their place, by destroying them ﴿تَبْدِيلًا﴾ emphasis (tawkīd). إِذَا has taken the place of إِنْ, as in "If He wills, He can remove you", because He, exalted is He, has not willed that, whereas إِذَا is for what will happen.

celaleyn:29-29.t: ﴿إِنَّ هَذِهِ﴾ sura ﴿تَذْكِرَةٌ﴾ an admonition for creation; ﴿فَمَنْ شَاءَ اتَّخَذَ إِلَى رَبِّهِ سَبِيلًا﴾ a way, through obedience.

celaleyn:30-30.t: ﴿وَمَا تَشَاءُونَ﴾ with tāʾ and with yāʾ — taking the way through obedience — ﴿إِلَّا أَنْ يَشَاءَ اللَّهُ﴾ that; ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ عَلِيمًا﴾ of His creation ﴿حَكِيمًا﴾ in His action.

celaleyn:31-31.t: ﴿يُدْخِلُ مَنْ يَشَاءُ فِي رَحْمَتِهِ﴾ His Paradise, and they are the believers; ﴿وَالظَّالِمِينَ﴾ what makes it accusative is an implied verb, i.e. أَعَدَّ, explained by ﴿أَعَدَّ لَهُمْ عَذَابًا أَلِيمًا﴾ painful; and they are the unbelievers.

daas-irab:1-1.t: ﴿هَلْ أَتى﴾ an interrogative particle for arousing interest (tashwīq), and a past verb; and ﴿عَلَى الْإِنْسانِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; and ﴿حِينٌ﴾ fāʿil (agent) of أتى; and ﴿مِنَ الدَّهْرِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted adjective (ṣifa) of حين; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position. And ﴿لَمْ يَكُنْ﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by lam, and its noun is latent (mustatir); and ﴿شَيْئاً﴾ khabar (predicate) of يكن; and ﴿مَذْكُوراً﴾ an adjective; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:2-2.t: ﴿إِنَّا خَلَقْنَا الْإِنْسانَ﴾ inna and its noun, and a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of إنا, and the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; and ﴿مِنْ نُطْفَةٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; and ﴿أَمْشاجٍ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of نطفة; and ﴿نَبْتَلِيهِ﴾ an imperfect verb and its mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). And ﴿فَجَعَلْناهُ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its first mafʿūl bihi; and ﴿سَمِيعاً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi; and ﴿بَصِيراً﴾ an adjective; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it.

daas-irab:3-3.t: ﴿إِنَّا هَدَيْناهُ﴾ inna and its noun, and a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and ﴿السَّبِيلَ﴾ its second mafʿūl bihi; the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of إنا, and the nominal clause is causal (taʿlīl), with no grammatical position; and ﴿إِمَّا﴾ a particle of condition and detailing (sharṭ wa-tafṣīl); and ﴿شاكِراً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَإِمَّا كَفُوراً﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it.

daas-irab:4-4.t: ﴿إِنَّا أَعْتَدْنا﴾ inna and its noun, and a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of إنا, and the nominal clause is resumptive; and ﴿لِلْكافِرِينَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; and ﴿سَلاسِلَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَأَغْلالًا وَسَعِيراً﴾ both conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes them.

daas-irab:5-5.t: ﴿إِنَّ الْأَبْرارَ يَشْرَبُونَ﴾ inna and its noun, and an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); and ﴿مِنْ كَأْسٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted adjective (ṣifa) of an omitted mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of inna, and the nominal clause is resumptive; and ﴿كانَ مِزاجُها كافُوراً﴾ kāna, its noun and its predicate; the clause is an adjective of كأس.

daas-irab:6-6.t: ﴿عَيْناً﴾ badal (substitute) of كافورا; and ﴿يَشْرَبُ﴾ an imperfect verb; and ﴿بِها﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; and ﴿عِبادُ اللَّهِ﴾ fāʿil (agent), annexed to the Name of Majesty; the verbal clause is an adjective (ṣifa) of عينا; and ﴿يُفَجِّرُونَها﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial); and ﴿تَفْجِيراً﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).

daas-irab:7-7.t: ﴿يُوفُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); and ﴿بِالنَّذْرِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is resumptive; and ﴿وَيَخافُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; and ﴿يَوْماً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it; and ﴿كانَ شَرُّهُ مُسْتَطِيراً﴾ kāna, its noun and its predicate; the clause is an adjective (ṣifa) of يوما.

daas-irab:8-8.t: ﴿وَيُطْعِمُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); and ﴿الطَّعامَ﴾ first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it; and ﴿عَلى حُبِّهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; and ﴿مِسْكِيناً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi; and ﴿يَتِيماً وَأَسِيراً﴾ both conjoined to what precedes them.

daas-irab:9-9.t: ﴿إِنَّما نُطْعِمُكُمْ﴾ restraining and restrained (kāffa wa-makfūfa), and an imperfect verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is the object of an implied saying (maqūl qawl muqaddar); and ﴿لِوَجْهِ اللَّهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb, and the Name of Majesty is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); and ﴿لا﴾ negative; and ﴿نُرِيدُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; and ﴿مِنْكُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; and ﴿جَزاءً﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَلا﴾ negative; and ﴿شُكُوراً﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to جزاء.

daas-irab:10-10.t: ﴿إِنَّا نَخافُ﴾ inna and its noun, and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); and ﴿مِنْ رَبِّنا﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; and ﴿يَوْماً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and ﴿عَبُوساً﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of يوما; and ﴿قَمْطَرِيراً﴾ a second adjective; the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of إنا, and the nominal clause is causal (taʿlīl).

daas-irab:11-11.t: ﴿فَوَقاهُمُ اللَّهُ﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, and a past verb and its first mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the Name of Majesty is fāʿil (agent); and ﴿شَرَّ ذلِكَ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi, annexed to the demonstrative; and ﴿الْيَوْمِ﴾ badal (substitute) of the demonstrative; the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَلَقَّاهُمْ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to فوقاهم. ﴿نَضْرَةً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi; and ﴿سُرُوراً﴾ conjoined to نضرة.

daas-irab:12-12.t: ﴿وَجَزاهُمْ﴾ a past verb and its first mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it; and ﴿بِما صَبَرُوا﴾ the bāʾ is a preposition, and mā is maṣdar-forming (maṣdariyya), and a past verb and its fāʿil; the interpreted maṣdar formed from mā and the verb is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by the bāʾ, and the preposition [with its genitive noun] is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; and ﴿جَنَّةً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi; and ﴿حَرِيراً﴾ conjoined to جنة.

daas-irab:13-13.t: ﴿مُتَّكِئِينَ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative (manṣūb); and ﴿فِيها﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) what precedes them; and ﴿عَلَى الْأَرائِكِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl from the latent (mustatir) pronoun in متكئين. And ﴿لا﴾ negative; and ﴿يَرَوْنَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); and ﴿فِيها﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; and ﴿شَمْساً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; and ﴿لا زَمْهَرِيراً﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to شمسا; the clause is a ḥāl.

daas-irab:14-14.t: ﴿وَدانِيَةً﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to متكئين; and ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) دانية; and ﴿ظِلالُها﴾ fāʿil (agent) of دانية; and ﴿وَذُلِّلَتْ﴾ a passive past verb; and ﴿قُطُوفُها﴾ nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); and ﴿تَذْلِيلًا﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); the clause is conjoined to دانية.

daas-irab:15-15.t: ﴿وَيُطافُ﴾ a passive imperfect verb; and ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; and ﴿بِآنِيَةٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; and ﴿مِنْ فِضَّةٍ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of آنية; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿وَأَكْوابٍ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿كانَتْ﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb whose noun is latent (mustatir); and ﴿قَوارِيرَا﴾ its khabar (predicate); the verbal clause is an adjective of أكواب.

daas-irab:16-16.t: ﴿قَوارِيرَا﴾ badal (substitute) of what precedes it; and ﴿مِنْ فِضَّةٍ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of قوارير; and ﴿قَدَّرُوها﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and ﴿تَقْدِيراً﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:17-17.t: ﴿وَيُسْقَوْنَ﴾ a conjunction, and a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); and ﴿فِيها﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; and ﴿كَأْساً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it; and ﴿كانَ مِزاجُها زَنْجَبِيلًا﴾ kāna, its noun and its predicate; the clause is an adjective (ṣifa) of كأسا.

daas-irab:18-18.t: ﴿عَيْناً﴾ badal (substitute) of زنجبيلا; and ﴿فِيها﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of عينا; and ﴿تُسَمَّى﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir); and ﴿سَلْسَبِيلًا﴾ second mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is a second adjective of عينا.

daas-irab:19-19.t: ﴿وَيَطُوفُ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ); and ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; and ﴿وِلْدانٌ﴾ fāʿil (agent); and ﴿مُخَلَّدُونَ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of ولدان; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. And ﴿إِذا﴾ a conditional adverb of time that does not make jussive; and ﴿رَأَيْتَهُمْ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by annexation; and ﴿حَسِبْتَهُمْ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its first mafʿūl bihi; and ﴿لُؤْلُؤاً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi; and ﴿مَنْثُوراً﴾ an adjective of لؤلؤا; the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:20-20.t: ﴿وَإِذا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; and ﴿إِذا﴾ a conditional adverb of time that does not make jussive; and ﴿رَأَيْتَ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by annexation; and ﴿ثَمَّ﴾ an adverb of place; and ﴿رَأَيْتَ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; and ﴿نَعِيماً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَمُلْكاً﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to نعيما; and ﴿كَبِيراً﴾ an adjective (ṣifa); the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:21-21.t: ﴿عالِيَهُمْ﴾ an adverb of place, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate); and ﴿ثِيابُ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), annexed to ﴿سُندُسٍ﴾; and ﴿خُضْرٌ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of ثياب; the nominal clause is resumptive; and ﴿إِسْتَبْرَقٌ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ثياب. ﴿وَحُلُّوا﴾ the wāw is of ḥāl (circumstantial), and a passive past verb and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); and ﴿أَساوِرَ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and ﴿مِنْ فِضَّةٍ﴾ an adjective of أساور; the clause is a ḥāl clause. ﴿وَسَقاهُمْ﴾ a past verb and its first mafʿūl bihi; and ﴿رَبُّهُمْ﴾ fāʿil (agent); and ﴿شَراباً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi; and ﴿طَهُوراً﴾ an adjective of شرابا; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:22-22.t: ﴿إِنَّ هذا كانَ﴾ inna and its noun, and a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb whose noun is latent (mustatir); and ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate). ﴿جَزاءً﴾ khabar; the clause of kāna is the khabar of inna, and the clause is the object of an omitted saying (maqūl qawl maḥdhūf). ﴿وَكانَ سَعْيُكُمْ مَشْكُوراً﴾ kāna, its noun and its predicate; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it.

daas-irab:23-23.t: ﴿إِنَّا﴾ inna and its noun; and ﴿نَحْنُ﴾ a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl); and ﴿نَزَّلْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of إنا, and the nominal clause is resumptive; and ﴿عَلَيْكَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; and ﴿الْقُرْآنَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and ﴿تَنْزِيلًا﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).

daas-irab:24-24.t: ﴿فَاصْبِرْ﴾ the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa and an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); and ﴿لِحُكْمِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; and ﴿رَبِّكَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, with no grammatical position. And ﴿وَلا تُطِعْ﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by lā, whose fāʿil is latent; and ﴿مِنْهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; and ﴿آثِماً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and ﴿أَوْ﴾ a conjunction; and ﴿كَفُوراً﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to آثما; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:25-25.t: ﴿وَاذْكُرِ﴾ an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); and ﴿اسْمَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object), annexed to ﴿رَبِّكَ﴾, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿بُكْرَةً﴾ an adverb of time. ﴿وَأَصِيلًا﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to بكرة; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:26-26.t: ﴿وَمِنَ اللَّيْلِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) اسجد; and ﴿فَاسْجُدْ﴾ the fāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), and an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); and ﴿لَهُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; and ﴿وَسَبِّحْهُ﴾ an imperative verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil is latent; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it; and ﴿لَيْلًا﴾ an adverb of time; and ﴿طَوِيلًا﴾ an adjective (ṣifa).

daas-irab:27-27.t: ﴿إِنَّ هؤُلاءِ يُحِبُّونَ﴾ inna and its noun, and an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); and ﴿الْعاجِلَةَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of inna, and the nominal clause is causal (taʿlīl). ﴿وَيَذَرُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil. ﴿وَراءَهُمْ﴾ an adverb of place; and ﴿يَوْماً﴾ mafʿūl bihi; and ﴿ثَقِيلًا﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of يوما; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it.

daas-irab:28-28.t: ﴿نَحْنُ خَلَقْناهُمْ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject), and a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَشَدَدْنا أَسْرَهُمْ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿وَإِذا﴾ a conditional adverb of time that does not make jussive; and ﴿شِئْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by annexation; and ﴿بَدَّلْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; and ﴿أَمْثالَهُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; and ﴿تَبْدِيلًا﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:29-29.t: Its i'rab has preceded in verse 19 of Sūrat al-Muzzammil.

daas-irab:30-30.t: ﴿وَما﴾ negative; and ﴿تَشاؤُنَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive; and ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿أَنْ يَشاءَ اللَّهُ﴾ an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an, and the Name of Majesty is the fāʿil; the interpreted maṣdar formed from an and the verb is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by annexation to an omitted adverb, i.e. «except at the time of Allah's willing»; and ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ كانَ﴾ inna and its noun, and a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb whose noun is latent (mustatir); and ﴿عَلِيماً حَكِيماً﴾ two predicates (khabar); the verbal clause is the khabar of inna, and the nominal clause is causal (taʿlīliyya).

daas-irab:31-31.t: ﴿يُدْخِلُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); and ﴿مَنْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial); and ﴿يَشاءُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; and ﴿فِي رَحْمَتِهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of من. ﴿وَالظَّالِمِينَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi of an omitted verb, its implied form being «He punishes» (يعذب); the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it; and ﴿أَعَدَّ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent; and ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; and ﴿عَذاباً﴾ mafʿūl bihi; and ﴿أَلِيماً﴾ an adjective (ṣifa); the clause is explicative (mufassira) of what precedes it.

dervis-irab:13-22.t:
* Vocabulary:
(زَمْهَرِيراً) In al-Mukhtār: «al-zamharīr is intense cold. I say: Thaʿlab said that al-zamharīr is also the moon in the dialect of Ṭayyiʾ, and by this he explained His saying, the Exalted: لا يرون فيها شمسا ولا زمهريرا, i.e. there is in it so much light and radiance that with it they need neither sun nor moon.»
And Abū Ḥayyān's wording: «al-zamharīr is the most intense cold. Thaʿlab said: it is the moon in the dialect of Ṭayyiʾ, and he recited the saying of the rajaz poet:
وليلة ظلامها قد اعتكر ... قطعتها والزمهرير ما ظهر
(And many a night whose darkness had thickened I traversed, while the moon had not appeared.)»
And al-Zamakhsharī's wording: «It means that its air is temperate: no heat of a sun that scorches, and no intensity of cold that harms. And in the ḥadīth: the air of Paradise is sajsaj (mild), neither heat nor cold.»
(قَوارِيرَا) The qārūra is a clear vessel in which drinks are placed; it is said that it is made of glass.
(زَنْجَبِيلًا) Ginger (al-zanjabīl): al-Dīnawarī said: a plant in the land of ʿUmān, roots that spread; it is not a tree; it is eaten fresh, and the best of it is what is carried from the lands of China. The Arabs loved it because it causes a sting on the tongue when it is mixed with drink, and they took pleasure in it. The poet said:
كأن القرنفل والزنجبي ... ل باتا بفيها وأريا مشورا
(As though clove and ginger had spent the night in her mouth, and gathered honey.)
And al-Musayyab ibn ʿAlas said:
وكأن طعم الزنجبيل به ... إذ ذقته وسلافة الخمر
(As though the taste of ginger were in it when I tasted it, and the first-pressed wine.)
The pronoun in به refers to the mouth, and إذ ذقته means: when I tasted its saliva; so it is figurative. And سلافة الخمر is the first that is pressed from grapes. Others said: al-zanjabīl is a plant with roots that spread in the earth, and knots of pungent taste grow in them; these roots branch out from a plant like reeds.
(سَلْسَبِيلًا) al-salsabīl: that which goes down the throat easily. Al-Zajjāj said: «In the language it is a description of what is utterly smooth-flowing.» Al-Zamakhsharī said: «One says a drink that is salsal, salsāl and salsabīl; the bāʾ was added in the composition until the word became five-lettered and indicated the utmost smoothness.» Ibn al-Aʿrābī said: «I have not heard al-salsabīl except in the Qur'an.» Makkī said: «It is a foreign, indefinite noun, and for that reason it is declined as a triptote.» The pattern of سلسبيل is like دردبيس; and it is said it is faʿfalīl because the fāʾ is repeated. Ṭalḥa read سلسبيل without nunation, and it was made a diptote for being a proper name and feminine, since it is the name of a specific spring. On this basis, how was it declined in the reading of the generality? The answer is that it was named so not as a proper name but as a mere general designation, or that it belongs to the category of the nunation of سلاسل and قوارير, as has preceded and as will come.
(سُندُسٍ) al-sundus is the fine kind of silk; it may be green or other than green.
(إِسْتَبْرَقٌ) al-istabraq is the thick kind of brocade; it forms the linings, and the sundus the outer faces.

* I'rab:
(مُتَّكِئِينَ فِيها عَلَى الْأَرائِكِ لا يَرَوْنَ فِيها شَمْساً وَلا زَمْهَرِيراً) متكئين is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the object of جزاهم. Abū al-Baqāʾ erred and allowed it to be a naʿt (adjective) of جنة; I do not know how this occurred to his mind, and my astonishment increased when I saw al-Zamakhsharī allowing it. He said: «It is permissible to make متكئين, لا يرون and دانية all adjectives of جنة.» That is rejected because the pronoun is not made overt, as it must be for a causal adjective (naʿt sababī); he did not say «متكئين هم فيها». And فيها is a ḥāl, i.e. in Paradise; على الأرائك is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) متكئين. The clause لا يرون is a second ḥāl of the object of جزاهم; you may also make it a ḥāl of the pronoun in متكئين, so that it is an overlapping ḥāl (ḥāl mutadākhila), just as you may make it an adjective of جنة as Abū al-Baqāʾ and al-Zamakhsharī determined. فيها is attached to يرون, شمسا is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and ولا زمهريرا is conjoined to شمسا. (وَدانِيَةً عَلَيْهِمْ ظِلالُها وَذُلِّلَتْ قُطُوفُها تَذْلِيلًا) Conjoined to متكئين, so the same considerations apply to it. The wāw entered to indicate that the two matters are combined for them, as if it were said: and He rewarded them with a Garden, combining in it safety from heat and cold and the nearness of the shades over them. You may make it accusative by conjunction to the position of لا يرون. Al-Zajjāj said it is an adjective of the جنة that is pronounced. As for Abū al-Baqāʾ, he went far afield, parsing it as an adjective of an omitted جنة, i.e. «and a Garden near», which is an artificiality and an arbitrary judgment with no justification. عليهم is attached to دانية, and على must be given the sense of من, because دنوّ is not made transitive with على; it did not say منهم only because the shades are high above them. The wāw is a conjunction, and ذللت is a past verb, passive, conjoined to دانية. The verbal clause was conjoined to the nominal one, contrary to pattern, only to indicate that the shading is a permanent matter that does not cease, because there is no sun in it, unlike the bringing-low (of the fruit clusters), which is a renewed, occurring matter. قطوفها is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) and تذليلا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). (وَيُطافُ عَلَيْهِمْ بِآنِيَةٍ مِنْ فِضَّةٍ وَأَكْوابٍ كانَتْ قَوارِيرَا) The wāw is a conjunction; يطاف is an imperfect verb, passive; عليهم is attached to يطاف; and بآنية is the deputy of the object, because it is the direct object in meaning. It is also permissible that عليهم be the deputy, with بآنية attached to يطاف. آنية is the plural of إناء; its origin is أأنية with two hamzas, the first added for the plural and the second the fāʾ of the word; the second was obligatorily changed into an alif. This is analogous to كساء and أكسية, غطاء and أغطية, and its analogue among words with a sound final radical is حمار and أحمرة.
من فضة is an adjective of آنية; أكواب is conjoined to آنية, as a conjunction of the specific to the general. The clause كانت is an adjective of أكواب; the noun of كانت is latent (mustatir), referring to the أكواب, and قواريرا is the khabar (predicate) of كانت. It is also permissible that كانت be complete (tāmma), so that قواريرا is a ḥāl, i.e. «they were brought into being». Abū al-Baqāʾ's wording: «Both are read with nunation and without nunation, and most pause on the first with an alif because it is the head of a verse.» [Translator's note: the closing quotation mark of Abū al-Baqāʾ's quotation is missing in the source; it is placed here as the most likely end.] (قَوارِيرَا مِنْ فِضَّةٍ قَدَّرُوها تَقْدِيراً) قوارير is a badal (substitute) of the first قواريرا, and it has been made a diptote; من فضة is an adjective of قوارير, and the clause قدّرت [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse has قدّروها] is a second adjective; تقديرا is an absolute object. قوارير was also read in the nominative on the implication of a mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. «they are قوارير». The meaning of the measuring is that they were prepared according to the measure of the drinkers' quenching, i.e. their desire, since there is no thirst in Paradise, without increase or decrease, and that is the most delightful drink. (وَيُسْقَوْنَ فِيها كَأْساً كانَ مِزاجُها زَنْجَبِيلًا) The wāw is a conjunction; يسقون is an imperfect verb, passive, and the wāw is the deputy agent; فيها is attached to يسقون; كأسا is the second object; the clause كان is an adjective of كأسا; مزاجها is the noun of كان and زنجبيلا its predicate. (عَيْناً فِيها تُسَمَّى سَلْسَبِيلًا) عينا is a substitute of زنجبيلا. It is said: their cup is mixed with ginger itself, or Allah creates its taste in it; on this view عينا is a substitute of كأسا, or accusative by specification (ikhtiṣāṣ), and perhaps this is the more likely. In any case, the aspects that apply to the first عينا apply to it. فيها is an adjective of عينا; the clause تسمى is a second adjective, its deputy agent latent, implied as «it»; and سلسبيلا is a second object. (وَيَطُوفُ عَلَيْهِمْ وِلْدانٌ مُخَلَّدُونَ إِذا رَأَيْتَهُمْ حَسِبْتَهُمْ لُؤْلُؤاً مَنْثُوراً) The wāw is a conjunction; يطوف is an imperfect verb; عليهم is attached to يطوف; ولدان is the fāʿil (agent); مخلدون is an adjective of ولدان. إذا is an adverb for future time, and the clause رأيتهم is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it. The clause حسبتهم has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition. حسبتهم is a past verb, its agent and its object; لؤلؤا is the second object and منثورا an adjective, i.e. scattered. In al-Miṣbāḥ: «I scattered it (nathartuhu), nathran, of the patterns of qatala and ḍaraba: I threw it scattered, and it became scattered.» (وَإِذا رَأَيْتَ ثَمَّ رَأَيْتَ نَعِيماً وَمُلْكاً كَبِيراً) The wāw is a conjunction; إذا is an adverb for future time containing the sense of condition; the clause رأيت is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it. رأيت is a verb and its agent; it has no object, overt or implied, so as to make the seeing widespread and general, as if it were said: and when seeing is brought into being there. ثمّ is an adverb of place, specific to the far, attached to ثمّ [Translator's note: so in the source; presumably "attached to رأيت" is meant]. The meaning is: and when seeing issues from you in that place, you see. The clause رأيت has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. نعيما is the object of the second رأيت, and ملكا كبيرا is conjoined to نعيما. Al-Farrāʾ said ثمّ is the object of رأيت, the implied form being «and when you see what is there»; ما was omitted and ثمّ stood in its place; and there is no need for this artificiality. (عالِيَهُمْ ثِيابُ سُندُسٍ خُضْرٌ وَإِسْتَبْرَقٌ) عاليهم: there are two aspects in its parsing. The first is that it is an adverb of place, because it means «above them». Abū Ḥayyān objected to this parsing and said: «عال and عالية are active participles, so for them to be adverbs it would need to be transmitted from the speech of the Arabs: عاليك or عاليتك a garment.» This objection is rejected, because words of the active-participle forms have come as adverbs, such as خارج الدار and داخلها, باطنها and ظاهرها; you say «I sat خارج الدار», and likewise the rest; so this is the same. Once this is established, the adverb is attached to an omitted fronted predicate; ثياب سندس is a delayed subject; خضر is an adjective of ثياب; and إستبرق is conjoined to ثياب with the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. «garments of istabraq». إستبرق was also read in the genitive by conjunction to سندس, because the meaning is: garments of sundus and garments of istabraq. The second aspect, which most follow, is that it is a ḥāl of the pronoun in يطوف عليهم, or of the object of حسبتهم, or of an implied muḍāf, i.e. «you saw the people of bliss and a great kingdom, above them...», so عاليهم is a ḥāl of the implied أهل. Al-Zamakhsharī mentioned this view, and his wording is: «And عاليهم in the accusative as a ḥāl of the pronoun in يطوف عليهم or in حسبتهم, i.e. there circulate among them youths, there being above those served garments; or you would think them scattered pearls, there being above them garments. And it is possible that the people of bliss be meant.» عاليهم was also read with a quiescent yāʾ and a kasra on the hāʾ, as a fronted predicate with ثياب a delayed subject, as if it were said: above them are garments. As for the text of Abū al-Baqāʾ's parsing, it is: «His saying, the Exalted: عاليهم: there are two views on it. One is that it is an agent-noun (fāʿil), made accusative as a ḥāl of the genitive noun in عليهم, and ثياب سندس is nominative by it, i.e. they are circulated among in the state of the sundus being high; and عاليهم was not made feminine because the femininity of الثياب is not real. The second view is that it is an adverb, because عاليهم is their skins, and there is weakness in this view. It is read with a quiescent yāʾ, either as a lightening of the accusative defective noun (manqūṣ), or as subject and predicate. And it is read عاليتهم with a tāʾ, which is clear. خضر in the genitive as an adjective of سندس and in the nominative of ثياب; and إستبرق in the genitive conjoined to سندس and in the nominative to ثياب.» I do not know how Abū al-Baqāʾ found it palatable to deem the adverb aspect weak, when the matter in it is lighter than with the ḥāl, given that it (عاليهم) comes as definite, whatever is said in its interpretation. (وَحُلُّوا أَساوِرَ مِنْ فِضَّةٍ وَسَقاهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ شَراباً طَهُوراً) Conjoined to ويطوف عليهم. Conjoining the past to the imperfect is allowed because it is future in meaning, and to announce its certainty. حلّوا is a past verb, passive, and the wāw is the deputy agent; أساور is the second object, and it is said it is accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), because they make it transitive to one object. من فضة is an adjective of أساور; سقاهم is conjoined to حلّوا; ربهم is the agent; شرابا is the second object, and طهورا an adjective of شرابا. (إِنَّ هذا كانَ لَكُمْ جَزاءً وَكانَ سَعْيُكُمْ مَشْكُوراً) The clause is the speech of an omitted saying, i.e. it is said to the people of Paradise. إنّ and its noun; the clause كان is its predicate; لكم is attached to جزاء; the noun of كان is latent, implied as «it», and جزاء is its predicate. And كان is conjoined to the first كان; سعيكم is its noun and مشكورا its predicate.

dervis-irab:23-31.t:
* I'rab:
(إِنَّا نَحْنُ نَزَّلْنا عَلَيْكَ الْقُرْآنَ تَنْزِيلًا) إنّ and its noun; نحن is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) or a tawkīd (emphasis) of the noun of إنّ; the clause نزلنا is the khabar (predicate) of إنّا; عليك is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) نزلنا; القرآن is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and تنزيلا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). You may also make نحن a mubtadaʾ (subject), so that the clause نزلنا is the predicate of نحن and the whole clause is the predicate of إنّ. (فَاصْبِرْ لِحُكْمِ رَبِّكَ وَلا تُطِعْ مِنْهُمْ آثِماً أَوْ كَفُوراً) The fāʾ is the faṣīḥa (fāʾ that discloses an omitted condition), i.e. if you know this, then be patient. اصبر is an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), implied as «you»; لحكم ربك is attached to اصبر. The wāw is a conjunction; لا is prohibitive; تطع is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لا, its agent latent, implied as «you»; منهم is a ḥāl (circumstantial); آثما is the direct object; أو is a conjunction, and كفورا is conjoined to آثما. He inclined to «أو» rather than the wāw only to convey the prohibition of obeying both of them together; had He conjoined with the wāw, it would have conveyed the permissibility of obeying one of them, which is not intended. Al-Zajjāj's wording: «أو here is more emphatic than the wāw, because if you said "do not obey Zayd and ʿAmr" and he obeyed one of them, he would not be disobedient; but if you replace it with أو, you have indicated that each one of them deserves to be disobeyed.» And Abū Ḥayyān's wording: «The prohibition of obeying each one of them is more eloquent than the prohibition of obeying both, because it entails the prohibition of one of them, since in obeying both there is obeying one of them; and if he said "do not strike Zayd and ʿAmr", it could be a prohibition of striking them both together, not of striking one of them. Abū ʿUbayda said «أو» means the wāw. And al-kafūr, even if he is a sinner (āthim), has in him an intensiveness in disbelief; and since the description kafūr differs from the one described by mere sin, the distinction was valid and the conjunction was apt.» (وَاذْكُرِ اسْمَ رَبِّكَ بُكْرَةً وَأَصِيلًا) Conjoined to what preceded. اذكر is an imperative verb; اسم ربك is the direct object; بكرة and أصيلا are two adverbs attached to اذكر. What is meant is constancy in prayer at its times. (وَمِنَ اللَّيْلِ فَاسْجُدْ لَهُ وَسَبِّحْهُ لَيْلًا طَوِيلًا) ومن الليل is attached to اسجد, and the meaning of من is partition, i.e. prostrate and pray to Him for part of the night. اسجد is an imperative verb, its agent latent, implied as «you»; له is also attached to اسجد. سبّحه is an imperative verb, a latent agent and a direct object; ليلا is an adverb attached to سبّحه, and طويلا is a naʿt (adjective). (إِنَّ هؤُلاءِ يُحِبُّونَ الْعاجِلَةَ وَيَذَرُونَ وَراءَهُمْ يَوْماً ثَقِيلًا) The clause is a causal explanation of the prohibition and command before it. The wording of al-Shihāb al-Khafājī: «This is a causal explanation of the prohibition and command before it, in His saying ولا تطع up to here; it is as if He said: do not obey them, and occupy yourself with what is more important, namely worship, because these people left the Hereafter for the world, so you leave the world and its people for the Hereafter. The first is a reason for the prohibition of obeying the sinner and the disbeliever, and the second a reason for the command to obey.» [Translator's note: the source does not close this quotation; its end is placed here as the most likely point.] إنّ is a particle resembling the verb; هؤلاء is a demonstrative, indeclinable (mabnī) on the kasra, in the position of the accusative as its noun; the clause يحبون is its predicate; العاجلة is the direct object; يذرون is conjoined to يحبون; وراءهم is an adverb of place meaning «in front», attached to an omitted ḥāl of the object, placed before it; يوما is the direct object and ثقيلا is an adverb [Translator's note: so in the source («ظرف»); ثقيلا is evidently an adjective of يوما]. The meaning of the heaviness will come in the section on rhetoric. (نَحْنُ خَلَقْناهُمْ وَشَدَدْنا أَسْرَهُمْ) نحن is the subject and the clause خلقناهم its predicate; شددنا is conjoined to خلقناهم, and أسرهم is the direct object, i.e. We strengthened their frame. al-asr, as in al-Qāmūs: «strength and anger, and firmness of physique and of constitution; and شددنا أسرهم means their joints.» And in al-Mukhtār: «asarahu, of the pattern of ḍaraba, i.e. he bound him with the isār, of the pattern of al-izār, which is the qidd (with kasra), a thong cut from untanned leather; and from it the captive (al-asīr) was named, because they used to bind him with the qidd, so everyone taken was called a captive even if not bound with it. And asarahu Allāh: He created him, of the pattern of ḍaraba; and from it: وشددنا أسرهم, i.e. their creation. And al-usr (with ḍamma) is retention of urine, like ḥaṣr in defecation. And the usra of a man is his family, because he is strengthened by them.» (وَإِذا شِئْنا بَدَّلْنا أَمْثالَهُمْ تَبْدِيلًا) The wāw is a conjunction; إذا is a future adverb containing the sense of condition; the clause شئنا is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it; the clause بدّلنا has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition; أمثالهم is the direct object and تبديلا is an absolute object. The second object of بدّلنا, since it means «We made», is omitted, its implied form being «in exchange for them». Now, al-Zamakhsharī got himself into an entanglement which he could have avoided: he said «Its proper form is that إن be used, not إذا, as in His saying: وإن تتولوا يستبدل قوما غيركم, إن يشأ يذهبكم», and he did not follow that with anything, thus giving the false impression that he means the Qur'an's use of إذا came contrary to what is right. In fact إذا and إن alternate with each other. They have said: إذا is for what is certain and إن for what is possible, and He, the Exalted, did not will it, so the apparent course is that إن be used; but إذا may be put in the place of إن and إن in the place of إذا, as in His saying: أفإن متّ فهم الخالدون. (إِنَّ هذِهِ تَذْكِرَةٌ فَمَنْ شاءَ اتَّخَذَ إِلى رَبِّهِ سَبِيلًا) إنّ and its noun, the reference being to the sūra; تذكرة is its predicate. The fāʾ is a conjunction; من is conditional, a subject; شاء is a past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the object of شاء is omitted, i.e. good for himself and a fine outcome. اتخذ is a past verb in the position of the jussive as the apodosis; إلى ربه is in the place of the second object, and سبيلا is the first object of اتخذ. (وَما تَشاؤُنَ إِلَّا أَنْ يَشاءَ اللَّهُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ كانَ عَلِيماً حَكِيماً) The wāw is a conjunction; ما is negative; تشاءون is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the agent; the object is omitted, i.e. obedience. إلا is a particle of restriction, and the interpreted maṣdar أن يشاء الله is in the position of the accusative as an adverb, because it is an exception from the most general of adverbs; its origin is «except at the time of Allah's willing». Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed the exception to be from the most general of states, so that the maṣdar is a ḥāl. إنّ and its noun; the clause كان is its predicate; the noun of كان is latent; عليما is its first predicate and حكيما its second predicate. (يُدْخِلُ مَنْ يَشاءُ فِي رَحْمَتِهِ وَالظَّالِمِينَ أَعَدَّ لَهُمْ عَذاباً أَلِيماً) The clause is a ḥāl of Allah. يدخل is an imperfect verb, nominative, and its agent is «He»; من is the direct object; the clause يشاء is the ṣila (relative clause) of من; في رحمته is attached to يدخل. والظالمين: the wāw is a conjunction, and الظالمين is accusative by an implied verb explained by what follows; Abū al-Baqāʾ implied it as:
«and He punishes the wrongdoers». The clause أعدّ is explicative; لهم is attached to أعدّ; عذابا is the direct object and أليما an adjective.

* Rhetoric:
In His saying «يوما ثقيلا» there is an explicit metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya): heaviness was borrowed for the severity and terror of that day from the heavy thing that is burdensome to its bearer; similar is ثقلت في السموات والأرض.

An error and a misplaced analogy:
It is laughable that one of them commented on His saying «وسبّحه ليلا طويلا» and said: this verse is a refutation of what the scholars of ʿilm al-maʿānī and al-bayān said, that combining ḥāʾ and hāʾ, for example, takes the word out of its eloquence (faṣāḥa); and they counted among that the saying of Abū Tammām:
كريم متى أمدحه أمدحه والورى ... معي وإذا ما لمته لمته وحدي
(A generous man: whenever I praise him, I praise him with all mankind joining me; and whenever I blame him, I blame him alone.)
This is an error on the part of the critic, who thought he was clearing the Noble Qur'an of defects that impair eloquence by condemning what the scholars of rhetoric established, and a misplaced analogy. The difference between the verse and the poetry is clear: it is the repetition of أمدحه that took it out of the path of eloquence, not the mere combination of ḥāʾ and hāʾ. Hence the verse is free of dissonance of letters (tanāfur al-ḥurūf). Shaykh Makhlūf al-Mīnāwī said in his gloss on Shaykh Aḥmad al-Damanhūrī's commentary on the text of Imām al-Akhḍarī: «The source of the heaviness is the repetition of أمدحه, not the mere combination, since it occurs between ḥāʾ and hāʾ in the Revelation, as in فسبّحه.»

* Benefits:
«إن» and «إذا» share in conveying that the occurrence of the consequence in the future is made dependent on the occurrence of the condition in it. But the basis of إن, i.e. the place of its real use, is doubt about the occurrence of the condition — it is said, and also mere supposition, and it is said, and likewise what is thought likely. And the basis of إذا is certainty of its occurrence. إن is not used other than for doubt, nor إذا other than for certainty, except for a subtle point (nukta), just as they do not enter upon a past verb, whether of condition or consequence, except for a subtle point, even if (wa-law) to make the occurrence of the content of the consequence dependent on the occurrence of the content of the condition. [Translator's note: the last clause is translated as written; «ولو» may be a misprint for «لو», i.e. "as لو does, which makes …".]

dervis-irab:1-12.t:
* Vocabulary:
(أَمْشاجٍ): mixtures, i.e. from the fluid of the man and the fluid of the woman, mingled and blended. A plural occurs as an adjective of a singular, i.e. of نطفة, because it has the meaning of a plural, or because each part of the drop was made a drop, and this was taken into account, so it was described with a plural. In al-Mukhtār: «مشج بينهما: he mixed [them]; its class is ضرب; the thing is مشيج, and the plural is أمشاج, like يتيم and أيتام. One says نطفة أمشاج for the man's fluid mixed with the woman's fluid and her blood». Al-Zamakhsharī's wording: «نطفة أمشاج is like برمة أعشار (a pot in pieces) and برد أكباش (a garment of coarse yarn); these are singular words, not plurals, and for that reason they occur as adjectives of singulars. One also says نطفة مشج. Al-Shammākh said:
طوت أحشاء مرتجة لوقت ... على مشج سلالته مهين
(She folded, in a womb closed for a time, upon a mixed drop whose essence is lowly.)
أمشاج cannot properly be a broken plural of it; rather both are alike in being singular, since a singular is described by both. مشجه and مزجه have the same meaning. The meaning is: from a drop in which the two fluids were blended».
(كافُوراً): الكافور is a fragrant plant. Its derivation seems to be from الكفر, which is covering, because it covers things with its scent. الكافور is also the sheath of trees which covers their fruit.
(مُسْتَطِيراً): spreading, widespread, reaching the utmost extent; from استطار الحريق (the fire spread) and استطار الفجر (the dawn spread). It stands to طار as استنفر stands to نفر. One says استطار يستطير استطارة, so it is مستطير; it is استفعل from الطيران (flying). Al-Farrāʾ said: «المستطير is المستطيل (the elongated)», as though he means it is like it in meaning, except that rāʾ was substituted for its lām. The dawn is two dawns: the elongated one, like the tail of the wolf, which is the false dawn; and the spreading one (مستطير), which is the true dawn, because it spreads across the horizon.
(قَمْطَرِيراً): القمطرير is the intensely frowning one who draws together what is between his eyes. Al-Zajjāj said: one says قمطرت الناقة when the she-camel raises her tail, draws together her two sides and wrinkles [Translator's note: the source has «وزقت», apparently for «وزمّت»] her nose; he derived it from القطر and made the mīm redundant. Asad ibn Nāʿiṣa said:
واصطليت الحروب في كل يوم ... باسل الشر قمطرير الصباح
(I have warmed myself at wars on every day grim in evil, frowning at morning.)
In al-Qāmūs: «يوم قماطر, like علابط, and قمطرير: severe; اقمطرّ: it became severe».

* I'rab:
(هَلْ أَتى عَلَى الْإِنْسانِ حِينٌ مِنَ الدَّهْرِ لَمْ يَكُنْ شَيْئاً مَذْكُوراً): there are two views on هل. First, it means قد ("indeed"). Second, it is interrogative in its proper sense, the question here being for affirmation (taqrīr) and rebuke. Al-Samīn's wording: «There are two views on this هل. First, that it is in its proper sense of pure interrogation. Makkī said, in establishing that it is in its proper sense of interrogation whose meaning is affirmation: it is an affirmation addressed to whoever denies the resurrection; he must say: Yes, a long age passed in which there was no human being. Then it is said to him: Who brought him into being after he was not, and his existence after his non-existence — how could his resurrection and revival after his death be impossible for Him? This is the meaning of His saying: ولقد علمتم النشأة الأولى فلولا تذكرون, i.e. why then do you not remember, and so know that whoever originated something after it was not is able to restore it after its death and non-existence. So he made it for the interrogative of affirmation, not for pure interrogation; and this is what must be so, because a question does not come from Allah the Exalted except in this way and the like. Second, that it means قد». As for al-Zamakhsharī, he said: «هل means قد, specifically in interrogation, and its origin is أهل, as evidenced by his saying: «أهل رأونا بسفح القاع ذي الأكم». So the meaning is "there has indeed come", by way of affirmation and nearness together, i.e. there came upon man, a short time ago…». As for the half-verse al-Zamakhsharī cited, it is the second hemistich of the verse:
سائل فوارس يربوع بشدتنا ... أهل رأونا بسفح القاع ذي الأكم
(Ask the horsemen of Yarbūʿ about our onslaught: did they see us at the foot of the hillocked plain?)
The verse is by Zayd al-Khayl, whom the Prophet ﷺ named Zayd al-Khayr. سائل is an imperative verb meaning "ask them, and press them with the question so that you may be certain of the true state of affairs". Yarbūʿ is the ancestor of a tribe. The bāʾ means عن, i.e. ask them about our strength. The basic interrogative particle is the hamza, which is why it has full right to stand first in speech; and the origin of هل is in the sense of قد, but because of frequent use in it [as an interrogative] the hamza became utterly forgotten and fell into disuse. The question here is for affirmation. أتى is a past verb; على الإنسان is attached (mutaʿalliq) to أتى; حين is the fāʿil (agent), and من الدهر is a naʿt (adjective) of حين. The clause لم يكن has two views. First, it is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الإنسان, i.e. "has there come upon him a time while he was in this state?". Second, it is in the position of nominative as an adjective of حين after an adjective; on this view the referring pronoun is omitted, its implied form being "a time in which he was not a thing mentioned". The first is preferable. Al-Zamakhsharī's wording: «If you ask: what is the position of لم يكن شيئا مذكورا? I say: its position is accusative as a ḥāl from الإنسان, as though it were said: has there come upon him a time of the age when he was unmentioned; or nominative as a description of حين, like His saying يوما لا يجزي والد عن ولده». لم is a particle of negation, inversion [to the past] and jussive; يكن is a deficient (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لم; its noun is latent (mustatir), its implied form being هو, referring to man; شيئا is its khabar (predicate), and مذكورا is an adjective of شيئا.
(إِنَّا خَلَقْنَا الْإِنْسانَ مِنْ نُطْفَةٍ أَمْشاجٍ نَبْتَلِيهِ): a resumptive statement brought to explain how man was created. إنّ and its noun; the clause خلقنا الإنسان is its khabar; من نطفة is attached to خلقنا, and أمشاج is an adjective of نطفة. The secret of a plural occurring as an adjective of a singular was given in the Vocabulary section; Abū al-Baqāʾ, however, allowed it to be a badal (substitute) of نطفة. The clause نبتليه has two views. First, it is a ḥāl from the agent of خلقنا, i.e. "We created him while testing him". Second, it is a ḥāl from الإنسان; this is valid because the clause contains two pronouns, each referring to the one the ḥāl qualifies. This ḥāl, moreover, may be concurrent (muqārina), if the meaning is "We test him by turning him about in his mother's womb, a drop then a clinging clot", or anticipated (muqaddara), if the meaning is "We test him, try him, with legal obligation", since at the time of his creation he is not under obligation.
(فَجَعَلْناهُ سَمِيعاً بَصِيراً):
The fāʾ is a conjunction for sequence with immediacy; جعلناه is a verb, its agent and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); سميعا بصيرا is the second direct object. The two words have been treated as a single word, because they are a kināya (metonymy) for discernment and understanding, since their organs are the cause of that, and they are the noblest of the senses, by which the greatest objects of perception are perceived. That is: on account of the test, when he became fit for it, We made him hearing and seeing, so that he could witness the proofs and hear the signs. So the conjunction is on the intention to test, not the test itself; and thus the following question does not arise: how was what follows conjoined to نبتليه with fāʾ when the test comes after it?
(إِنَّا هَدَيْناهُ السَّبِيلَ إِمَّا شاكِراً وَإِمَّا كَفُوراً): the clause gives the reason for the test. إنّ and its noun; the clause هديناه — verb, agent and object — is the khabar of إنا; السبيل is a second direct object, or in the position of accusative by removal of the preposition, [the implied] preposition and its genitive noun being attached to هديناه. إما is a particle of condition and detailing; شاكرا and كفورا are two ḥāls from the hāʾ in هديناه, i.e. We enabled him and empowered him for both his states; or We called him to Islam by the proofs of reason and of revelation, it being known whether he would believe or disbelieve, in order to establish the proof against him. They may also be two ḥāls from السبيل, i.e. We made known to him either a grateful way or an ungrateful way, like His saying وهديناه النجدين; describing the way with gratitude and ingratitude is then figurative. The secret of the contrast between the active participle and the intensive form will come in the Rhetoric section.
(إِنَّا أَعْتَدْنا لِلْكافِرِينَ سَلاسِلَ وَأَغْلالًا وَسَعِيراً): the clause also gives a reason, because when He mentioned the two groups He followed them with the threat and the promise. إنّ and its noun; the clause أعتدنا is its khabar; للكافرين is attached to أعتدنا; سلاسل is a direct object, prevented from taking full declension (a diptote) because it is a plural on the pattern مفاعل. It was also read as fully declined (سلاسلًا), for consonance with أغلالا; both are readings among the Seven. Abū Ḥayyān's wording: «Ṭalḥa, ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd, Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr and Ḥamza read سلاسل as a diptote, in pause and in continuation; it has been reported of Ḥamza and Abū ʿAmr that they paused with alif. Ḥafṣ and Ibn Dhakwān read it as a diptote, and there is disagreement in the reports from them about the pause, and likewise from al-Bazzī. The rest of the Seven read it with tanwīn in continuation and with the alif substituted for it in pause, and this is the reading of al-Aʿmash. It has been said that this follows what al-Akhfash related of the dialect of those who decline fully everything that is diptote except أفعل; it is the usage of the poets, which then became frequent until it ran in their [ordinary] speech. It has been explained that
since this plural is itself pluralized — they said صواحبات يوسف and نواكسي الأبصار — it resembled the singular, so full declension was applied to it. One of the rajaz poets said:
والصرف في الجمع أتى كثيرا ... حتى ادّعى قوم به التخييرا
(Full declension in the plural has come often, until some claimed there is free choice in it.)»
(إِنَّ الْأَبْرارَ يَشْرَبُونَ مِنْ كَأْسٍ كانَ مِزاجُها كافُوراً): إنّ and its noun; the clause يشربون is its khabar; من كأس is attached to يشربون, and the object of يشربون is omitted, i.e. "wine from a cup". الكأس is the glass when there is wine in it, and the wine itself is called كأس. Al-Aʿshā said:
وكأس شربت على لذة ... وأخرى تداويت منها بها
(Many a cup I drank with pleasure, and another with which I cured myself of it.)
The clause كان مزاجها كافورا is an adjective of كأس; كان, its noun and its khabar.
(عَيْناً يَشْرَبُ بِها عِبادُ اللَّهِ يُفَجِّرُونَها تَفْجِيراً): the grammarians have expanded on the ways of parsing عينا, and the views they have given reach seven. We give them briefly below and then proceed to the preference. 1- A substitute of كافورا, because its water is like camphor in whiteness, scent and coolness. 2- A substitute of the position of من كأس; on this view al-Zamakhsharī implied the omission of a muḍāf, saying: «as though it were said: they drink in it wine, the wine of a spring». Abū al-Baqāʾ, however, made the muḍāf implied on the view of substitution from كافورا, saying: «The second: a substitute of كافورا, i.e. the water of a spring or the wine of a spring». 3- The object of يشربون, i.e. they drink a spring from a cup. 4- Accusative by specification (ikhtiṣāṣ). 5- Accusative by an implied يشربون explained by what follows it, as Abū al-Baqāʾ also said. 6- Accusative by a concealed verb, its implied form being يعطون ("they are given"). 7- Accusative as a ḥāl from the pronoun in مزاجها, as Makkī said. We consider the first and the fourth the most preferable views and the nearest to ease, though that does not preclude acknowledging the soundness of all the views we have cited. The clause يشرب is an adjective of عينا; بها is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يشرب, and the pronoun refers to the cup [Translator's note: so in the source; al-Zamakhsharī's explanation that follows takes it as referring to the spring], i.e. they drink the spring with that cup, the bāʾ being for adhesion (ilṣāq). Al-Zamakhsharī said: «If you ask: why was the verb of drinking connected first with the particle of beginning, and last with the particle of adhesion?
I say: because the cup is the starting point of their drinking and the first of its extent, whereas the spring is that with which they mix their drink; so the meaning is as though: the servants of Allah drink wine with it, as you say "I drank water with honey"». It has also been said that the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), i.e. يشربها, and the reading يشربها, with the verb made transitive to the pronoun by itself, indicates this. [It has also been said] that it means من, so that it is partitive; al-Aṣmaʿī, Ibn Mālik, al-Fārisī and al-Qutabī affirmed this, and counted among its examples this verse and His saying, the Exalted, فامسحوا برءوسكم; on it al-Shāfiʿī built his doctrine of wiping part of the head in ablution, because of the proofs that were established for him. It may also be in the position of accusative as a ḥāl, i.e. "mixed". It may also be that يشربون carries the sense of "they take delight in it, drinking", or carries the sense of يرتوي, i.e. the servants of Allah quench their thirst with it. The clause يفجرونها is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl, i.e. they make it flow wherever they wish from their dwellings, so it is easy and does not resist them; or it is a second adjective of عينا. تفجيرا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).
(يُوفُونَ بِالنَّذْرِ وَيَخافُونَ يَوْماً كانَ شَرُّهُ مُسْتَطِيراً): an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī), as though it were asked: by what did they deserve this bliss? And it was said: they fulfil…. يوفون is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the agent; بالنذر is attached to يوفون; يوما is a direct object; the clause كان is an adjective of يوم; شره is the noun of كان, and مستطيرا its khabar.
(وَيُطْعِمُونَ الطَّعامَ عَلى حُبِّهِ مِسْكِيناً وَيَتِيماً وَأَسِيراً): conjoined to يوفون and يخافون. الطعام is a direct object; على حبه is attached to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. "loving it"; على means مع ("with"), i.e. for accompaniment. حبه is a maṣdar (verbal noun) annexed to its object, so the pronoun is for the food, i.e. while desiring it and needing it; similar is «وآتى المال على حبه». The pronoun may also properly refer to Allah, i.e. out of love of Allah, that is, for His Face and seeking His good pleasure. The first is more praiseworthy, because in it there is preferring others over oneself, and food is loved by the poor and the rich, whereas on the second view the rich may do it more. مسكينا is the second direct object and what follows it is conjoined to it. These were singled out for mention for a secret that will come in the Rhetoric section.
(إِنَّما نُطْعِمُكُمْ لِوَجْهِ اللَّهِ لا نُرِيدُ مِنْكُمْ جَزاءً وَلا شُكُوراً): the clause gives the reason, explaining the cause of the feeding. إنما is [إنّ] restraining and restrained (kāffa wa-makfūfa); نطعمكم is an imperfect verb, a latent agent, its implied form being نحن, and a direct object; لوجه الله is attached to نطعمكم. The clause لا نريد… is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); لا is negative; نريد is an imperfect verb whose agent is latent, its implied form being نحن; منكم is attached to نريد; جزاء is a direct object, and ولا شكورا is conjoined to it.
(إِنَّا نَخافُ مِنْ رَبِّنا يَوْماً عَبُوساً قَمْطَرِيراً): giving the reason for His saying إنما نطعمكم. إنّ and its noun; the clause نخاف is its khabar; the agent of نخاف is a latent pronoun, its implied form being نحن; من ربنا is attached to نخاف; يوما is a direct object; عبوسا is an adjective and قمطريرا a second adjective of يوما.
(فَوَقاهُمُ اللَّهُ شَرَّ ذلِكَ الْيَوْمِ وَلَقَّاهُمْ نَضْرَةً وَسُرُوراً): the fāʾ is a conjunction to show the cause, i.e. because of their fear Allah protected them, that is, warded off from them the evil of that Day and its pressure. وقاهم is a past verb and a fronted direct object; الله is a postponed agent; شر is a second direct object; ذلك is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and اليوم is a substitute of the demonstrative. لقاهم is a past verb, a latent agent and a direct object; نضرة is a second direct object, and سرورا is conjoined to نضرة.
(وَجَزاهُمْ بِما صَبَرُوا جَنَّةً وَحَرِيراً): جزاهم is also conjoined; جزاهم is a past verb, a latent agent and a direct object; بما is attached to جزاهم; ما is maṣdariyya, i.e. "for their patience"; جنة is a second direct object, and حريرا is conjoined to جنة.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His saying «إنّا هديناه السبيل إما شاكرا وإما كفورا»: since few people are characterized by gratitude, He said شاكرا, expressing it by the active participle to indicate its rarity; and since many are characterized by ingratitude and it occurs frequently from man, He said كفورا, expressing it by the intensive form.
2- In His saying «ويطعمون الطعام على حبه مسكينا ويتيما وأسيرا», these three were singled out for mention because the needy person is unable to earn his own sustenance; the orphan's parents, who are the ones who earn, have died, and he is left unable to earn because of his young age; and the captive has no power over harm or benefit for himself, nor any help or means. ʿAṭāʾ said:
This verse came down concerning ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib. He hired himself out one night to water date-palms for some barley, until morning. He received the barley, and they ground a third of it and made something from it to eat. When it was fully cooked, a needy man came, so they brought out the food to him. Then the next third was prepared [Translator's note: the source has «ثم صنع الثلث الباقي», "then the remaining third was prepared", though two thirds remained at this point], and when it was fully cooked an orphan came, and they fed him. Then the third [third], and when it was fully cooked a captive from among the polytheists came and asked, and they fed him; and they went hungry that day. So Allah sent down these verses about them.
3- In His saying «إنّا نخاف من ربنا يوما عبوسا قمطريرا» there is a predicative metaphor (majāz isnādī), of which many parallels have preceded in this book, because describing the day as frowning is figurative, as it is said "his day is fasting and his night is standing [in prayer]", the people of them being meant.

* Benefits:
1- «كان» in the Qur'an has five aspects:
1- In the sense of eternity without beginning and without end, as in «وكان الله عليما حكيما».
2- In the sense of the past that has ended, as in «وكان في المدينة تسعة رهط».
3- In the sense of the present, as in «كنتم خير أمة».
4- In the sense of the future, as in «ويخافون يوما كان شره مستطيرا».
5- In the sense of صار ("became"), as in «وكان من الكافرين».
2- إمّا has five meanings:
1- Doubt, as in: "Either Zayd or ʿAmr came to me", when you do not know which of them came.
2- Deliberate vagueness (ibhām), as in «وآخرون مرجون لأمر الله إما يعذبهم وإما يتوب عليهم», i.e. Allah the Exalted knows the reality of their state, and vagueness towards the hearer is intended.
3- Choice (takhyīr), as in «إما أن تعذب وإما أن تتخذ فيهم حسنا»; it occurs only after a request, so [a request] is implied in the verse, the original being: "O Dhū al-Qarnayn, act: either punish…".
4- Permission (ibāḥa), as in: "Learn either jurisprudence or grammar".
5- Detailing (tafṣīl), as in: «إنّا هديناه السبيل إما شاكرا وإما كفورا».

farraa:1-1.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿هَلْ أَتَىٰ عَلَى ٱلإِنسَانِ حِينٌ مِّنَ ٱلدَّهْرِ﴾.
Its meaning: there has indeed (قد) come upon man a period of time. "هل" may be a denial (jaḥd), and it may be a statement (khabar).
This is of the statement kind; because you may say: "Did I not admonish you (فهل وعظتك)? Did I not give you (فهل أعطيتك)?", making him affirm that you did give him and admonish him. The denial is when you say: "And can anyone (وهل يقدر واحد) do the like of this?"
His saying, Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿لَمْ يَكُن شَيْئاً مَّذْكُوراً﴾.
He means: he was a thing, but he was not something mentioned. That is from the time Allah created him from clay until He breathed the spirit into him.

farraa:2-2.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَمْشَاجٍ نَّبْتَلِيهِ﴾.
الأمشاج: the mixtures — the man's fluid, the woman's fluid, the blood and the clot. When something of this sort [117/b] is mixed it is called مشيج, as you say خليط (mixed), and ممشوج, as you say مخلوط (mixed).
His saying: ﴿نَّبْتَلِيهِ﴾ — the meaning, and Allah knows best, is: We made him hearing and seeing in order to test him. This is placed earlier while its meaning is later; the meaning is only: We created him and made him hearing and seeing in order to test him.

farraa:3-3.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿إِنَّا هَدَيْنَاهُ ٱلسَّبِيلَ﴾.
Also إلى السبيل and للسبيل; all of that is permissible in the speech of the Arabs. He says: We guided him, i.e. We made the way known to him, whether he is grateful or ungrateful. (إما) here may be conditional (jazāʾ), i.e.: whether he is grateful or whether he is ungrateful; or it may be the (إما) found in His saying: ﴿إِما يُعَذِّبُهُمْ وَإِمَّا يَتُوبُ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾, as though He said: We created him wretched or happy.

farraa:4-4.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿سَلاَسِلَ وَأَغْلاَلاً﴾.
"سلاسل" was written with an alif, and some of the readers declined it as a triptote (ajrāhā) because of the alif at its end, while some did not. The one who did not decline it said: the Arabs keep the alif in the accusative of what is a diptote (lā yujrā), and when they join it to what follows they drop the alif; and both are correct. Similar to that is His saying: ﴿كانَتْ قَوَارِيراً﴾ (15): the alif was kept in the first because it is the end of a verse, while the other is not [the end of] a verse. So keeping the alif in the first was stronger because of this argument, and that is how I saw it in the codex of ʿAbd Allāh; the people of Basra read it so and wrote it so in their codices. The people of Kufa and Medina keep the alif in both of them together, as though they found it strange for one word with one accusative meaning to be written in two different ways. If you wish, you decline both as triptotes; if you wish, you decline neither; and if you wish, you decline the first because of the alif in the writing of the people of Basra and do not decline the second, since it has no alif.

farraa:5-5.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَشْرَبُونَ مِن كَأْسٍ كَانَ مِزَاجُهَا كَافُوراً﴾.
It is said that it is a spring called al-Kāfūr. It may also be that its mixture is like camphor because of the fragrance of its scent, in which case it is not a name. The Arabs [118/a] put the accusative on whichever of these two words they like. Ḥassān said:
كأنَّ خبيئَةً من بيت رأْسٍ * يكونُ مِزاجُها عَسلٌ وماءُ
(As though a hidden [wine] from Bayt Raʾs, whose mixture is honey and water.)
It is clearer in meaning to make the verb [i.e. its accusative predicate] fall on المزاج, even though it is definite; and all is correct. You say: كان سيدَهم أبوك (your father was their chief) and كان سيدُهم أباك. The preferred way is to say: كان سيدَهم أبوك; because "father" is a fixed noun, whereas "chief" is one of the attributes.

farraa:6-6.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿عَيْناً﴾.
If you wish, you make it follow الكافور as an explicative of it; and if you wish, you put it in the accusative by detachment (qaṭʿ) from the hāʾ in "مزاجها".
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَشْرَبُ بِهَا﴾, and "يَشْرَبُهَا".
They are the same in meaning. It is as though يشرب بها means: quenches his thirst with it and slakes it. As for يشربونها, it is clear. Someone recited to me:
شَرِبْنَ بِمَاءِ البحرِ ثمَّ تَرَفَّعتْ * مَتى لُججٍ خُضْرٍ لَهُنَّ نئيجُ
(They drank of the sea's water, then rose up out of green deep waves, with a roaring sound.)
Similar to it is: إنه ليتكلم بكلام حسن, and يتكلم كلاماً حسناً (he speaks with fine speech / he speaks fine speech).
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يُفَجِّرُونَهَا تَفْجِيراً﴾.
Whichever [place] a man of the people of Paradise likes, he makes it gush forth for himself.

farraa:7-7.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يُوفُونَ بِٱلنَّذْرِ﴾.
This is one of their attributes in this world; it is as though there is an implied كان in it: they used to fulfil the vow.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيَخَافُونَ يَوْماً كَانَ شَرُّهُ مُسْتَطِيراً﴾.
Its trial is far-spreading. The Arabs say: the crack spread (استطار) in the glass flask and the like, and also استطال.

farraa:10-10.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿عَبُوساً قَمْطَرِيراً﴾.
القمطرير: the severe. One says: يوم قمطرير and يوم قماطر (a severe day). Someone recited to me:
بَنِى عمِّنا، هل تذكُرونَ بَلاءَنا * علَيكُمْ إذا ما كانَ قُمَاطِرُ
(O sons of our uncle, do you remember our good service to you when there was a severe [day]?)

farraa:13-13.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He [«عز وجلك» in the source — Translator's note: a typo for «عز وجل:»]: ﴿مُّتَّكِئِينَ فِيهَا﴾.
It is in the accusative as by detachment (qaṭʿ). If you wish, you make it follow الجنة, as though you said: their reward is a Garden, reclining in it.

farraa:14-14.t:
His saying, exalted be His mention: ﴿وَدَانِيَةً عَلَيْهِمْ ظِلاَلُهَا﴾.
It may be accusative on that [same pattern]: their reward is a Garden, reclining in it, and its shades being near. If you wish, you make الدانية follow المتكئين by way of detachment (qaṭʿ), which may also be nominative on [118/b] resumption (istiʾnāf). So it is permissible like His saying: ﴿وَهَذَا بَعْلِى شَيْخاً﴾ and "وشيخٌ". In the reading of Ubayy it is: "ودانٍ عليهم ظلالها", and this is resumptive, in the position of the nominative; and in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: "ودانياً عليهم ظلالها". The masculine and feminine forms of الداني are like His saying: ﴿خَاشِعاً أبْصَارُهم﴾ in one place and ﴿خاشعةً أبصارهم﴾ in another. الدانية may also be accusative on the pattern of the Arabs' saying: عند فلان جاريةٌ جميلةٌ، وشابةً بعدُ طريةً (So-and-so has a beautiful slave-girl, and young still, fresh), interposing praise parenthetically, without intending it to be coordinated with what precedes; it is as though they imply with this wāw a verb by which the accusative comes about, [as] in one of the two readings: "وحوراً عيناً". Someone recited to me:
ويأوى إلى نسوة عاطلاتٍ * وشُعثا مراضيعَ مثل السعالِى
(And he takes refuge with women bare of ornament, and dishevelled ones, nursing mothers, like ghouls.)
with the accusative, i.e.: وشعثا; though the genitive is more common.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَذُلِّلَتْ قُطُوفُهَا تَذْلِيلاً﴾.
The people of Paradise pick the fruit standing and sitting, and in every state, with no effort in it.

farraa:15-15.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كَانَتْ قَوَارِيرَاْ﴾.
He says: they had the clarity of glass and the whiteness of silver, so the clarity of glass and the whiteness of silver were combined in them.

farraa:16-16.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَدَّرُوهَا﴾.
They measured the cup to the thirst of each one of them, with nothing left over and nothing falling short of quenching his thirst; and that is the most delightful drink.
Some have transmitted from al-Shaʿbī: (قُدِّروها تَقْدِيراً). The meaning is the same, and Allah knows best: "it was measured for them" and "they measured it" are equivalent.

farraa:17-18.t:
His saying: ﴿كَأْساً كَانَ مِزَاجُهَا زَنجَبِيلاً﴾.
