It is only called a كأس when there is drink in it; when there is no wine in it, the name كأس does not apply to it.
I heard one of the Arabs say of the tray on which a gift is presented: it is the مِهْدَى, as long as the gift is on it; when it is [119/a] empty it reverts to its own name, whether it is a tray (طبق) or a table (خوان) or something else.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿زَنجَبِيلاً عَيْناً﴾.
It is mentioned that the ginger (الزنجبيل) is the spring, and that الزنجبيل is a name for it; and the same interpretation applies to it as to الكافور.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿تُسَمَّىٰ سَلْسَبِيلاً﴾.
They mentioned that السلسبيل is a name for the spring, and it is mentioned that it is a description of the water for its smooth flowing and its sweetness. We consider that if it were a name for the spring, leaving it undeclined (tark al-ijrāʾ, i.e. treating it as a diptote) would be more common; yet we have not seen any of the readers leave it undeclined, though that is permissible in Arabic, just as in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: ﴿وَلاَ تَذَرُنّ وَدًّا ولا سُوَاعاً ولا يَغُوثاً ويَعُوقاً﴾ with the alif, and as they said "سلاسلا" and "قواريرا" with the alif, declining as triptotes what is not declined. That is not a mistake, because the Arabs decline as triptotes in poetry what is not declined; if it were a mistake they would not have brought it into their poems. Mutammim ibn Nuwayra said:
فما وجد أظآرٍ ثلاثٍ روائمٍ * رأين مَجَرًّا من حُوارٍ ومصْرعَا
(The grief of three foster she-camels, tenderly attached, that saw where a young camel was dragged and where it fell, is not [like mine].)
So he declined روائم as a triptote, though it is one of those not declined — [this occurs] in more instances than I can count in their poems.

farraa:19-19.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مُّخَلَّدُونَ﴾.
He says: adorned and wearing bracelets; it is also said: wearing earrings; and it is said: مخلدون means their youth is everlasting, they do not change from that age. This is the most likely to be correct — and Allah knows best — because when a man grows old among the Arabs and the blackness of his hair remains, it is said: إنه لمخلد. Likewise, when he grows old and his teeth and molars remain [firm], it is said: إنه لمخلد, i.e. of unchanging condition.
Likewise the youths: their teeth remain [unchanged].

farraa:20-20.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِذَا رَأَيْتَ ثَمَّ رَأَيْتَ نَعِيماً﴾.
It is said: when you see what is there (ما ثَمّ), you see bliss; and implying (ما) is acceptable, just as it was said: ﴿لَقَدْ تَقَطَّعَ بَيْنَكُمْ﴾, the meaning being: what is between you, and Allah knows best. It is also said: إذا رأيت [119/b] ثم, meaning: when you look; then when you cast your sight there you see bliss.

farraa:21-21.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿عَالِيَهُمْ ثِيَابُ سُندُسٍ﴾.
Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, ʿĀṣim and al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī read it in the accusative, treating it like an adverb: "above them". The Arabs say: قومك داخلَ الدار (your people are inside the house), putting داخل الدار in the accusative because it is a place (maḥall); and عاليهم is of that kind. The people of the Ḥijāz and Ḥamza read: "عَالِيهم" with the yāʾ left unvowelled (irsāl), and in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is: "عاليتُهم ثيابُ سُنْدُسٍ" with tāʾ — and that is an argument for whoever leaves the yāʾ unvowelled and makes it quiescent. The readers differed over الخضر and السندس [Translator's note: so in the source; the context indicates خضر and إستبرق]: Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb put them both in the genitive, intending to make الخضر a description of السندس and ويكسر على الاستبرق [Translator's note: so in the source; apparently "and to make الاستبرق coordinate with it"] — ثيابُ سندس and ثيابُ استبرق. Al-Ḥasan put both words in the nominative, making الخضر a description of الثياب and putting الاستبرق in the nominative by coordinating it back onto الثياب. Some put الخضر in the nominative and الاستبرق in the genitive, and [others] put الاستبرق in the nominative and الخضر in the genitive; and all of that is correct. And Allah is praised.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿شَرَاباً طَهُوراً﴾.
He says: pure, not impure, as it [wine] was spoken of as impure in this world.

farraa:24-24.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلاَ تُطِعْ مِنْهُمْ آثِماً أَوْ كَفُوراً ﴾.
(وُ) [Translator's note: so in the source; read (أو)] here is equivalent to (لا). أو, in denial, interrogation and conditional (jazāʾ) [contexts], has the meaning of (لا), and this is one of those. The poet said:
لا وَجْدُ ثَكْلَى كما وَجِدْتُ وَلا * وَجْدُ عَجُولٍ أَضَلَّهَا رُبَعُ
أَوْ وَجْدُ شيخٍ أصَلَّ ناقَتهُ * يَوْمَ توافَى الحجيجُ فاندفعُوا
(Neither the grief of a bereaved mother is like the grief I felt, nor the grief of a she-camel that lost her young calf, or the grief of an old man who lost his she-camel on the day the pilgrims gathered and then pushed on.)
He meant: ولا وجد شيخ (nor the grief of an old man). In Arabic it may also be: do not obey among them anyone who sins or disbelieves.
Then the meaning of (أو) is close to the meaning of (الواو), as when you say to a man: لأعطينك سألت أو سكتّ (I will surely give to you, whether you ask or keep silent), meaning: I will surely give to you in any case.

farraa:28-28.t:
His saying [120/a], Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَشَدَدْنَآ أَسْرَهُمْ﴾.
الأسر: the make (الخلق). You say: لقد أُسِر هذا الرجل أحسنَ الأسر (this man has been made with the finest make), as you say: خُلِقَ أحسنَ الخَلْق (he was created with the finest creation).

farraa:29-29.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّ هَـٰذِهِ تَذْكِرَةٌ﴾.
He says: this sura is a reminder and an admonition. ﴿فَمَن شَآءَ ٱتَّخَذَ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِ سَبِيلاً﴾: a direction and a road to good.

farraa:30-30.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَا تَشَآءُونَ﴾.
A response to His saying: ﴿فَمَنْ شَاءَ اتّخذَ إلَى رَبِّهِ سَبِيلاً﴾.
Then He informed them that the matter is not up to them, and said: ﴿وَمَا تَشَآءُونَ﴾ that way ﴿إِلاَّ أَن يَشَآءَ ٱللَّهُ﴾ for you. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: ﴿وَمَا تَشَآءُونَ إِلاَّ أَن يَشَآءَ ٱللَّهُ﴾ [Translator's note: so in the source, identical to the standard reading; the following remark suggests ʿAbd Allāh's reading had (ما) in place of (أن), i.e. «إلا ما شاء الله»]. The meaning of (ما) and (أن) is close.

farraa:31-31.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلظَّالِمِينَ أَعَدَّ لَهُمْ﴾.
You put الظالمين in the accusative because the wāw in لها [Translator's note: so in the source; apparently "the lām in لهم" is meant] becomes like an adverbial container (ẓarf) for أعدّ. If it were nominative it would be correct, as He said: ﴿والشُّعَرَاءُ يَتَّبِعُهُمُ الْغَاوُونَ﴾ without hamza. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is: "وللظالمين أعد لهم", repeating the lām in (الظالمين) and in (لهم); and the Arabs sometimes do that. Someone recited to me:
أقول لها إذا سألت طلاقا * إلامَ تسارعين إلى فراقى
(I say to her, when she asks for divorce: to what end do you hasten to part from me?)
And someone recited to me:
فأصبحْنَ لا يَسلنهُ عن بما به * أصعَّد فى غاوى الهَوى أم تصوَّبا؟
(And by morning they would not ask him about what was with him: had he gone up in the error of passion, or come down?)
So he repeated the bāʾ twice [Translator's note: in the verse what is repeated is the preposition عن with ب]. Had he said: لا يسلنه عما به, it would have been clearer and better; but the poet sometimes adds and omits to complete the verse. If you directed the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿عَمَّ يَتَسَاءَلُونَ، عن النَّبَإِ الْعَظِيم﴾ to this interpretation, it would be correct in Arabic.
It has another interpretation, meaning: About what are they asking one another, O Muhammad! Then He informed and said: they are asking one another about the great news. Similar to this is His saying in al-Mursalāt: ﴿لأَِىِّ يَوْمٍ أُجِّلَتْ﴾ as an expression of wonder, then He said: ﴿ليوم الفصل﴾, i.e.: they were deferred to the Day of Decision.

harrat-mujtaba:1-1.t: The preposition and its genitive noun «من الدهر» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «حين»; the clause «لم يكن» is a naʿt of «حين», the linking element being implied (muqaddar), i.e.: in it (فيه).

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: The preposition and its genitive noun «من نطفة» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «خَلَقْنا»; «أمشاج» is a naʿt (adjective), and a plural came as the attribute of a singular because it has a plural meaning; the clause «نبتليه» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «خَلَقْنا»; the clause «فجعلناه» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «نبتليه»; «بصيرا» is a multiple mafʿūl bihi (direct object), because the khabar (predicate) may be multiple, and likewise what was originally a khabar.

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: «إما» is a particle of detailing; «شاكرا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ in «هديناه», i.e.: We guided him, both states having been made clear to him.

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: The clause «كان» is a naʿt (adjective) of «كأس».

harrat-mujtaba:6-6.t: «عينا» is a badal (substitute) from {كَافُورًا}; the clause «يشرب» is a naʿt (adjective) of «عينا»; and the clause «يُفَجِّرونها» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «يشرب».

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: The clause «يوفون» is resumptive; «يوما» is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause «كان» is a naʿt (adjective).

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: The preposition and its genitive noun «على حبه» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الطعام», i.e.: being in their love of food.

harrat-mujtaba:9-9.t: The preposition and its genitive noun «لوجه» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «نطعم»; the clause «لا نريد» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «نطعمكم»; the clause «إنما نطعمكم» is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl) of an implied (muqaddar) saying which is a ḥāl from the fāʿil of «يطعمون», i.e.: they give food, saying: we feed you only.

harrat-mujtaba:10-10.t: «يوما» is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); «قمطريرا» is a second attribute.

harrat-mujtaba:11-11.t: The clause «فوقاهم» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «نخاف»; «شرّ» is the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and «نضرة» is the second mafʿūl bihi.

harrat-mujtaba:12-12.t: The preposition and its genitive noun «بما»: «ما» is maṣdariyya (infinitival), i.e.: He rewarded them for their patience; «جنة» is a second object.

harrat-mujtaba:13-13.t: «متكئين» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ in «جزاهم»; the two preposition and its genitive nouns are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «متكئين»; and the clause «لا يَرَوْن» is a second ḥāl.

harrat-mujtaba:14-14.t: His words «ودانية»: a noun conjoined (maʿṭūf) to {مُتَّكِئِينَ}; the preposition and its genitive noun «عليهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «دانية»; «ودانية» includes the meaning of «مُشْرفة» (overlooking); «ظلالها» is the fāʿil (agent) of «دانية»; and the clause «ذُلِّلت قطوفها» is conjoined to the single word «دانية».

harrat-mujtaba:15-15.t: The clause «ويطاف» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «جزاهم» in verse (12); the preposition and its genitive noun «بآنية» is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the preposition and its genitive noun «عليهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يطاف»; the preposition and its genitive noun «من فضة» is attached to «آنية»; and the clause «كانت» is a naʿt (adjective) of «أكواب».

harrat-mujtaba:16-16.t: «قوارير» is a badal (substitute) from the first; the preposition and its genitive noun «من فضة» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «قوارير»; and the clause «قدَّروها» is a naʿt of the second «قوارير».

harrat-mujtaba:17-17.t: The preposition and its genitive noun «فيها» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb, and the clause «كان» is a naʿt (adjective) of «كأسا».

harrat-mujtaba:18-18.t: «عينا» is a badal (substitute) from {زَنْجَبِيلا}; the preposition and its genitive noun «فيها» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «عينا»; the clause «تسمى» is a naʿt of «عينا»; and «سلسبيلا» is a second object.

harrat-mujtaba:19-19.t: The clause «ويطوف» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «يسقون», and the conditional clause is a second naʿt (adjective) of «ولدان».

harrat-mujtaba:20-20.t: The conditional clause is resumptive; «ثَمَّ» is an adverb of place specific to the distant, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «رأيت» before it; the object of the seeing is not mentioned.

harrat-mujtaba:21-21.t: His words «عاليهم»: an accusative adverb of place, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) «ثياب»; it is not made feminine because the mubtadaʾ is figuratively feminine; «خضر» is a naʿt (adjective) of «ثياب»; the clause «وحُلُّوا» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the nominal clause «عاليهم ثياب»; «أساور» is a second object; the preposition and its genitive noun «من فضة» is attached to a naʿt of «أساور»; «شرابا» is a second object.

harrat-mujtaba:22-22.t: The preposition and its genitive noun «لكم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the maṣdar (verbal noun) «جزاء», and the second clause «كان» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the first.

harrat-mujtaba:23-23.t: «نحن» is tawkīd (emphasis) of the pronoun (نا) in «إنا».

harrat-mujtaba:24-24.t: The clause «فاصبر» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause {نَزَّلْنَا}; the preposition and its genitive noun «منهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «آثما».

harrat-mujtaba:25-25.t: «بكرة» is an adverb of time attached to (mutaʿalliq) «اذكر».

harrat-mujtaba:26-26.t: The wāw is a conjunction, and the preposition and its genitive noun is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «اسجد»; the fāʾ in «فاسجد» is redundant (zāʾida); the clause «اسجد» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the preceding clause «اذكر»; «ليلا» is an adverb of time attached to «سبِّحه».

harrat-mujtaba:27-27.t: «يوما» is mafʿūl bihi (direct object), not an adverb.

harrat-mujtaba:28-28.t: The conditional clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «شددنا»; «تبديلا» is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).

harrat-mujtaba:29-29.t: The conditional clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the resumptive clause «إن هذه تذكرة»; the preposition and its genitive noun «إلى ربه» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the second object of «اتخذ».

harrat-mujtaba:30-30.t: The clause «وما تشاءون» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «من شاء»; «إلا» is for restriction (ḥaṣr); the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) «أن يشاء» is accusative by removal of the preposition, the bāʾ.

harrat-mujtaba:31-31.t: The clause «يُدخل» is resumptive; his words «والظالمين»: the object of an implied (muqaddar) verb, [assumed] as «عاقَبَ» (He punished); the clause of the implied verb is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «يدخل», and the clause «أعدَّ» explains the implied verb.

mekki-muskil:1-1.t: His saying, the Exalted: (هل أتى على الإنسان): it is said that (هل) means (قد) "indeed". The better view is that (هل) is in its proper sense, the interrogative whose meaning is affirmation (taqrīr). It is only an affirmation addressed to whoever denies the resurrection: he cannot but say "Yes, a long stretch of time has passed in which there was no man." Then it is said to him: "Who brought him into being after he was not, and gave him existence after his non-existence? How then could his resurrection and his revival after his death be impossible for Him?" This is the meaning of His saying (ولقد علمتم النشأة الأولى فلولا تذكرون), i.e. "why then do you not remember", so that you know that whoever originated a thing after it was not, without a prior model, is able to restore it after its non-existence and its death.

mekki-muskil:3-3.t:
His saying (إما شاكرا وإما كفورا): two ḥāls (circumstantials) from the hāʾ. (سميع) and (بصير) — [(بصير)] is a naʿt (adjective) of (سميع) [Translator's note: so in the source]. (إما) is for choice (takhyīr), in its proper sense. The meaning of choice is that Allah informed us that He chose a people for felicity and a people for misery; so the meaning is that He creates him either felicitous or miserable. This is among the clearest indications that Allah the Exalted has decreed all things, and created a people for felicity, who do its deeds, and a people for misery, who do its deeds. So the choice is an announcement from Allah the Exalted that He chooses what He wills and does what He wills, making whom He wills grateful and whom He wills a disbeliever; the choice does not belong to man. It is also said that it is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara), the implied form being: either gratitude arises from him when he comes to understanding, which is the sign of felicity, or disbelief arises from him, which is the sign of misery; and all of that is according to what preceded in Allah the Exalted's knowledge concerning them. The Kufans allowed (ما) to be redundant (zāʾida) and (إن) to be conditional. This is not permissible according to the Basrans, because the conditional (إن) does not enter upon nouns, since nouns are not made to carry a condition, unless you imply a verb after (إن), in which case it is permissible, as in His saying, the Exalted: (وإن أحد من المشركين): "asks you for protection" (استجارك) is implied after (إن), and the second (استجارك) indicates it, so its omission is good. Implying a verb after (إن) is not possible here, because it would entail the nominative of (شاكر) and (كفور) by that verb; moreover, there is nothing in the speech indicating the implied verb. It is also said that in the verse there is a placing forward and back, the implied form being: "We created man from a mingled drop, testing him, either grateful or ungrateful, and made him hearing and seeing"; on this view they are two ḥāls from (الإنسان). This is a good view, so there is no choice for man in himself.
His saying (سلاسلا) and (قواريرا): the origin of all of it is to be a diptote, because it is a plural, and the plural is heavy; and because it is not pluralised further, so it differs from the other plurals; and because it has no counterpart among singulars; and because it is the utmost of plurals, since it is not pluralised further; so it is heavy and is a diptote. As for those readers who made it fully declinable, it is a dialect of some Arabs: al-Kisāʾī reported that they make fully declinable everything that is a diptote except (أفعل منك) "more ... than you". Al-Akhfash said: we heard from the Arabs some who make this and all diptotes fully declinable. It is also said that he made it declinable only because it occurs in the Muṣḥaf with an alif, so he made it declinable in following the script of the Muṣḥaf; and it was written in the Muṣḥaf with an alif only because they are verse endings, so they resemble rhymes and verse-end pauses, to which an alif is added for the pause. It is also said that he made it declinable only because it is a plural like the other plurals, which some Arabs pluralised like a singular, so it is declinable just as the singular is declinable. Do you not see the saying of the Prophet ﷺ to Ḥafṣa: «إنكن لأنتن صواحبات يوسف» ("You women are indeed the companions of Joseph"), where he pluralised (صواحب) with alif and tāʾ as the singular is pluralised, so it became declinable as the singular is? Al-Akhfash reported (مواليات فلان), pluralising (موالي), so it became like the singular. The grammarians recited, of al-Farazdaq:
.. وإذا الرجال رأوا يزيد رأيتهم ... خضع الرقاب نواكس الأبصار ...
(And when men see Yazīd, you see them with necks bowed and eyes cast down.)
They transmitted it with kasra on the sīn of (نواكس), making it the plural of (نواكس) with yāʾ and nūn; the nūn was dropped because of the annexation and the yāʾ because of the meeting of two vowelless letters, and the sīn remained with kasra in pronunciation. Its being pluralised shows that it is pluralised like the other plurals, and all plurals are declinable, so this one too was made declinable on that basis.

mekki-muskil:5-6.t: His saying (مزاجها كافورا عينا): (عينا) is accusative as a badal (substitute) from (كافور). It is also said: as a badal from (كأس) according to its position; also said: as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in (مزاجها); and also said: with an implied verb, i.e. "they drink a spring", i.e. the water of a spring, then the muḍāf was omitted. Al-Mubarrad said it is accusative with an implied "I mean" (أعني).

mekki-muskil:11-11.t: His saying (ذلك اليوم): (اليوم) is a naʿt (adjective) of (ذلك), or a badal (substitute) from it.

mekki-muskil:12-12.t: His saying (جنة وحريرا): accusative governed by (جزاهم) as a second object; the implied form is "entry into a garden and wearing of silk", then the muḍāf was omitted in both. (متكئين) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ and mīm in (جزاهم), and its governor is (جزى); (صبروا) does not govern it, because the patience was in this world while the reclining and the recompense are in the Hereafter. Likewise the position of (لا يرون) is also accusative as a ḥāl, like (متكئين), or as a ḥāl from the pronoun in (متكئين). It is not good for (متكئين) to be an adjective of (جنة), because that would require making overt the pronoun that is in (متكئين), since it would run as an adjective of something other than what it belongs to.

mekki-muskil:14-14.t: His saying (ودانية عليهم): (دانية) is accusative by conjunction with (جنة); it is an adjective standing in place of what it qualifies, its implied form being "and a garden near". It is also said that (دانية) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) conjoined to (متكئين) or to the position of (لا يرون). (الظلال) is nominative governed by (دانية) because it is the agent of the nearness. It has been read (ودانيا) in the masculine; it is masculine because of the separation, and it is also said: because of the masculine of the plural. It is permissible to put (دانية) in the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of (الظلال), so that (الظلال) is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause is in the position of a ḥāl from the hāʾ and mīm, or from the pronoun in (متكئين) if you make (لا يرون) a ḥāl from it. (دان) is also permissible, in the nominative and masculine, as mubtadaʾ and khabar, being masculine on the grounds stated above.

mekki-muskil:17-18.t:
His saying (ويسقون فيها كأسا كان مزاجها زنجبيلا عينا): (عينا) is accusative as a badal (substitute) from (كأس), or with an implied (يسقون), i.e. "they are given to drink the water of a spring", then the muḍāf was omitted; or with an implied "I mean" (أعني).
His saying (تسمى سلسبيلا): in (تسمى) there is an implied object whose agent is not named [nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent)], referring back to (العين), and (سلسبيلا) is a second object. It is a foreign indefinite noun, which is why it is fully declinable.

mekki-muskil:20-20.t: His saying (وإذا رأيت ثم رأيت): the first (رأيت) does not pass to an object according to most of the Basrans, and (ثم) is an adverbial of place. Al-Farrāʾ and al-Akhfash said that (ثم) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of (رأيت). Al-Farrāʾ said: its implied form is "And when you see what is there", so (ما) is the object; (ما) was omitted and (ثم) stood in its place. According to the Basrans it is not permissible to omit the relative and have its ṣila (relative clause) stand in its place.

mekki-muskil:21-21.t:
His saying (عاليهم ثياب): whoever reads it in the accusative takes it as an adverbial meaning "above them". It is also said that it is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in (لقاهم), or from the pronoun in (جزاهم), I mean the hāʾ and mīm. (ثياب) is nominative governed by (عاليهم) if you make it a ḥāl. If you make it an adverbial, you put (ثياب) in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) and (عاليهم) is the khabar (predicate), with a nominative pronoun in (عاليهم); or, if you wish, you put it in the nominative by the notion of being settled (istiqrār), with no pronoun in (عاليهم), because it then becomes like a verb placed before its agent; whereas if you put (ثياب) in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ, (عاليهم) is like a verb placed after its agent, so there is a pronoun in it. Whoever made the yāʾ in (عاليهم) vowelless put it in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ and (ثياب) as the khabar, (عالي) having the meaning of a group, as the Exalted said (سامرا تهجرون), bringing the singular form meaning the group; and likewise the Exalted said (فقطع دابر القوم), which is only "the hindmost ones (أدبار) of the people", the singular sufficing for the plural. It is also permissible for (ثياب) to be nominative by its verb[al force], because (عاليا) is an active participle; so it is a mubtadaʾ and (ثياب) is an agent standing in place of the khabar of (عاليهم). On this view (عال) is singular, not meaning the plural, as you say (قائم الزيدون) "the Zayds are standing", making it singular because it runs according to the rule of the verb that precedes, so it is singular since it has put what follows it in the nominative. This is the school of al-Akhfash. (عاليهم) is indefinite because separation is intended by it, since it has a future meaning; that is why its accusative as a ḥāl is permissible, and because it is indefinite, others than al-Akhfash disallowed putting it in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ.
His saying (خضر وإستبرق): whoever reads (خضر) in the genitive makes it a naʿt (adjective) of (سندس), and (سندس) is a collective noun; it is also said to be a plural whose singular is (سندسة); it is the fine kind of brocade. Whoever reads it in the nominative makes it a naʿt of (ثياب). Whoever reads (وإستبرق) in the nominative conjoins it to (ثياب), and whoever reads it in the genitive conjoins it to (سندس). (الإستبرق) is the thick kind of brocade. (إستبرق) is a foreign indefinite noun, which is why it is fully declinable, and its alif is a disjunctive alif (alif qaṭʿ) in foreign nouns. Ibn Muḥayṣin read it without declension, which is a mistake if he made it a noun, because it is a declinable indefinite. It is also said that, rather, he made it a past verb from (برق); this is permissible in wording but far-fetched in meaning. It is also said that in origin it is a past verb on the pattern istafʿala from (برق), so it is Arabic, from (البريق) "glitter"; when it was used as a name, its alif became disjunctive, because it is not the origin of nouns that the connective alif should enter them; it entered only into a limited number of weak nouns altered from their origin, on which no analogy is made.

mekki-muskil:23-23.t:
His saying (إنا نحن نزلنا): (نحن) is in the position of the accusative as an adjective of the noun of (إن), because a pronoun may be qualified by a pronoun, since that is in the sense of emphasis, not in the sense of description; it may not be qualified by an overt noun, because that is in the sense of description, and the pronoun has no need of description, since it is only made a pronoun after its description and identity are known; but it does need emphasis so that the predication about it may be confirmed. It is not permissible [Translator's note: so in the source; the context suggests «ويجوز» "it is permissible" was intended] for (نحن) to be a separating pronoun (fāṣila) with no position in i'rab and (نزلنا) the khabar (predicate). It is also permissible for (نحن) to be nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) and (نزلنا) the khabar, the clause being the khabar of (إن).
And His saying (ويذرون وراءهم يوما): (وراء) means "in front of" and "before". That is permissible in (وراء) because it carries the meaning of concealment: whatever is concealed from you, whether before you, in front of you or behind you, is called (وراء) because it is concealed from you. (يوما) is an object of (يذرون). We have already mentioned the origin of (يذرون) and its explanation.

mekki-muskil:24-24.t: His saying (آثما أو كفورا): (أو) is for permission (ibāḥa), i.e. "do not obey this kind". Al-Farrāʾ said: (أو) in this is like (لا), i.e. "do not obey whoever sins nor whoever disbelieves", and that is in the sense of the permission we mentioned. It is also said that (أو) means (و) "and", but that is far-fetched.

mekki-muskil:30-30.t: His saying (وما تشاءون إلا أن يشاء الله): (أن) is in the position of the accusative as an exception, or in the position of the genitive according to al-Khalīl's view with the preposition implied, and according to the view of others in the position of the accusative since the preposition has been omitted; its implied form is "except by Allah's willing". This has many parallels that preceded: we mentioned their i'rab once according to the view of al-Khalīl and Sībawayh and once according to the view of others, for brevity, and once we mentioned both views together, as a reminder.

mekki-muskil:31-31.t: His saying (والظالمين): accusative with an implied verb, i.e. "and He punishes the wrongdoers; He has prepared for them a punishment", because preparing punishment leads to punishment; that is why implying (يعذب) is good, since the context of the speech indicates it. It is not permissible to imply (أعد), because it only passes [to this object] by a preposition; in this and what resembles it, only a verb that passes without a preposition is implied, one indicated by the context of the speech and the purport of the address. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [Ibn Masʿūd]: (وللظالمين أعد لهم), with the genitive lām on (الظالمين), with the implied form "and for the wrongdoers He prepared — He prepared for them". The Kufans said: (والظالمين) is accusative only because the wāw with it is an adverbial for the verb, namely (أعد); and this is speech whose meaning cannot be made out. It is permissible to put (الظالمين) in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), with what follows as its khabar (predicate); al-Aṣmaʿī heard someone reading so, but it is not acted upon in the Qur'an because it differs from the script of the Muṣḥaf and from the body of the readers. Al-Farrāʾ made it, in the nominative, like His saying, the Exalted: (والشعراء يتبعهم الغاوون); but it is not like it, because before (والظالمين) there is a verb that governed an object, so the clause was conjoined to a clause, and it was necessary that the [noun of the] predication in the second clause be accusative, just as it was in the first clause, in His saying (يدخل من يشاء). Before His saying (والشعراء) there is a clause consisting of mubtadaʾ and khabar, so it was necessary that the second clause be likewise. So the nominative is the proper aspect in (الشعراء), and the accusative is permissible outside the Qur'an; and the accusative is the proper aspect in (والظالمين), and the nominative is permissible outside the Qur'an. This is a principle to be relied upon in this chapter.

muyesser-irab:1-1.t:
﴿هل﴾: there are two views on it: one of them, that it has the meaning of «قد» (indeed); and the second, that it is an interrogative in its proper sense, the interrogative here being for affirmation and reproach.
﴿أتى﴾: a past verb.
﴿على الإنسان﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أتى﴾.
﴿حين﴾: fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ).
﴿من الدهر﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of ﴿حين﴾.
﴿لم﴾: a particle of negation, conversion [of the imperfect to past meaning], and jussive.
﴿يكن﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm); its noun is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "huwa" (he).
﴿شيئا﴾: the khabar of kāna.
﴿مذكورا﴾: a naʿt; and regarding the clause «لم يكن» there are two views: one of them, that it is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الإنسان», i.e. "has a time come [upon him] in this state?"; and the second, that it is in the position of a nominative as a naʿt of ﴿حين﴾.

muyesser-irab:2-2.t:
﴿إنا﴾: resumptive speech, with no grammatical position; «إن» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and ﴿نا﴾ is its noun.
﴿خلقنا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause ﴿خلقنا الإنسان﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of «إن».
﴿الإنسان﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿من نطفة﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿خلقنا﴾.
﴿أمشاج﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿نطفة﴾, or a badal (substitute) from «نطفة».
﴿نبتليه﴾: an imperfect verb; the fāʿil is latent (mustatir), and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi; regarding the clause ﴿نبتليه﴾ there are two views: one of them, that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil of ﴿خلقنا﴾, i.e. "We created him while We were testing him"; and the second, that it is a ḥāl from «الإنسان».
﴿فجعلناه﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction for sequence with immediate succession, and «جعلناه» is a verb, its fāʿil, and mafʿūl bihi.
﴿سميعا﴾: ḥāl from the mafʿūl bihi.
﴿بصيرا﴾: a second ḥāl, accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa.

muyesser-irab:3-3.t:
﴿إنا﴾: «إن» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and ﴿نا﴾ is its noun; the clause is causal (taʿlīliyya) for what was begun with.
﴿هديناه﴾: a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and object; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of «إنّ».
﴿السبيل﴾: a second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), or in the position of an accusative by removal of the preposition, the preposition and its genitive noun [then] being attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿هديناه﴾.
﴿إما﴾: a particle of condition and detailing.
﴿شاكرا﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ in «هديناه».
﴿وإما﴾: a particle of condition and detailing.
﴿كفورا﴾: ḥāl from the hāʾ in ﴿هديناه﴾.

muyesser-irab:4-4.t:
﴿إنا﴾: «إن» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and ﴿نا﴾ is its noun; the clause is causal (taʿlīliyya) for what was begun with.
﴿أعتدنا﴾: a verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause «أعتدنا» is the khabar (predicate) of «إن».
﴿للكافرين﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أعتدنا﴾.
﴿سلاسل﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿وأغلالا﴾: conjoined to ﴿سلاسل﴾.
﴿وسعيرا﴾: conjoined to ﴿سلاسل﴾.

muyesser-irab:5-5.t:
﴿إن الأبرار﴾: «إن» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and «الأبرار» is its noun.
﴿يشربون﴾: a verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause «يشربون» is the khabar (predicate) of «إن».
﴿من كأس﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يشربون﴾; the object of «يشربون» is omitted, i.e. "wine from a cup".
﴿كان مزاجها﴾: «كان» is an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb, «مزاج» is its noun, and ﴿ها﴾ is muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿كافورا﴾: the khabar of kāna; the clause «كان مزاجها كافورا» is a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿كأس﴾.

muyesser-irab:6-6.t:
﴿عينا﴾: a badal (substitute) from ﴿كافورا﴾, or accusative by way of specification (ikhtiṣāṣ).
﴿يشرب﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ).
﴿بها﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يشرب﴾.
﴿عباد﴾: fāʿil (agent).
﴿الله﴾: the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿يفجرونها﴾: a verb, its fāʿil and object; the clause is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).
﴿تفجيرا﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).

muyesser-irab:7-7.t:
﴿يوفون﴾: resumptive speech with no grammatical position; «يوفون» is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent).
﴿بالنذر﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يوفون﴾.
﴿ويخافون﴾: conjoined to what precedes it; it is an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is the fāʿil.
﴿يوما﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿كان﴾: an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb.
﴿شره﴾: the noun of kāna.
﴿مستطيرا﴾: the khabar of kāna; the clause «كان» is an adjective (ṣifa) of ﴿يوم﴾.

muyesser-irab:8-8.t:
﴿ويطعمون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and [«يطعمون» is] a verb and its fāʿil (agent).
﴿الطعام﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿على حبه﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يطعمون﴾.
﴿مسكينا﴾: mafʿūl bihi.
﴿ويتيما﴾: maʿṭūf (conjoined) to ﴿مسكينا﴾.
﴿وأسيرا﴾: maʿṭūf to ﴿مسكينا﴾.

muyesser-irab:9-9.t:
﴿إنما﴾: the clause is a causal explanation (taʿlīl), and «إنما» is [«إنّ»] restrained by the restraining «ما» (kāffa wa-makfūfa).
﴿نطعمكم﴾: an imperfect verb, a latent fāʿil (agent), its implied form being "naḥnu" (we), and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿لوجه﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿نطعمكم﴾.
﴿الله﴾: the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿لا﴾: negating.
﴿نريد﴾: an imperfect verb; its fāʿil is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "naḥnu" (we); the clause ﴿لا نريد﴾ is a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause.
﴿منكم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿نريد﴾.
﴿جزاء﴾: mafʿūl bihi.
﴿ولا﴾: «لا» is negating.
﴿شكورا﴾: maʿṭūf (conjoined) to «جزاء».

muyesser-irab:10-10.t:
﴿إنا﴾: a causal explanation (taʿlīl); «إن» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and ﴿نا﴾ is its noun.
﴿نخاف﴾: an imperfect verb; the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "naḥnu" (we); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of «إن».
﴿من ربنا﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿نخاف﴾.
﴿يوما﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿عبوسا﴾: naʿt (adjective).
﴿قمطريرا﴾: a second naʿt of ﴿يوما﴾.

muyesser-irab:11-11.t:
﴿فوقاهم﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and «وقاهم» is a past verb and a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿الله﴾: the Name of Majesty, a postponed fāʿil (agent).
﴿شر﴾: a second mafʿūl bihi.
﴿ذلك﴾: muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿اليوم﴾: a badal (substitute) from the demonstrative.
﴿ولقاهم﴾: a past verb; the fāʿil is "huwa" (He); and a mafʿūl bihi.
﴿نضرة﴾: a second mafʿūl bihi.
﴿وسرورا﴾: conjoined to ﴿نضرة﴾.

muyesser-irab:12-12.t:
﴿وجزاهم﴾: a past verb; the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "huwa" (He); and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.
﴿بما﴾: the bāʾ is a preposition, and «ما» is causal (sababiyya).
﴿صبروا﴾: a past verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿جزاهم﴾.
﴿جنة﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿جزاهم﴾. [Translator's note: so in the source; ﴿جنة﴾ is not a preposition and its genitive noun — it is evidently the second object of «جزاهم», and the wording appears to have been carried over from the line above.]
﴿وحريرا﴾: conjoined to ﴿جنة﴾.

muyesser-irab:13-13.t:
﴿متكئين﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative (manṣūb), from the object of ﴿جزاهم﴾.
﴿فيها﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl.
﴿على الأرائك﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿متكئين﴾.
﴿لا﴾: negating.
﴿يرون﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the clause «لا يرون» is a second ḥāl from the object of ﴿جزاهم﴾, or a ḥāl from the pronoun in «متكئين».
﴿فيها﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يرون﴾.
﴿شمسا﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative.
﴿ولا﴾: negating.
﴿زمهريرا﴾: conjoined to ﴿شمسا﴾.

muyesser-irab:14-14.t:
﴿ودانية﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «دانية» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to ﴿متكئين﴾, accusative (manṣūb); or accusative by conjunction to the position of ﴿لا يرون﴾.
﴿عليهم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿دانية﴾.
﴿ظلالها﴾: the fāʿil (agent) of «دانية», nominative (marfūʿ).
﴿وذللت﴾: a past verb, passive (built for that whose agent is not named), and conjoined to ﴿دانية﴾.
﴿قطوفها﴾: nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
﴿تذليلا﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).

muyesser-irab:15-15.t:
﴿ويطاف﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «يطاف» is an imperfect verb, passive (built for that whose agent is not named).
﴿عليهم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يطاف﴾.
﴿بآنية﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
﴿من فضة﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of ﴿آنية﴾.
﴿وأكواب﴾: conjoined to ﴿آنية﴾.
﴿كانت﴾: an abrogating (nāsikh) past verb, the tāʾ being for the feminine; the noun of kāna is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "hiya" (it).
﴿قواريرا﴾: the khabar of kāna, accusative (manṣūb); the clause «كانت» is a naʿt of ﴿أكواب﴾.

muyesser-irab:16-16.t:
﴿قوارير﴾: a badal (substitute), accusative (manṣūb), from the first ﴿قوارير﴾.
﴿من فضة﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted naʿt (adjective) of ﴿قوارير﴾.
﴿قدروها﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause ﴿قدروها﴾ is a second naʿt.
﴿تقديرا﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).

muyesser-irab:17-17.t:
﴿ويسقون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «يسقون» is an imperfect verb, passive (built for that whose agent is not named), and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
﴿فيها﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يسقون﴾.
﴿كأسا﴾: a second mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause «كان» is an adjective (ṣifa) of ﴿كأسًا﴾.
﴿كان﴾: an abrogating (nāsikh) past verb.
﴿مزاجها﴾: the noun of kāna, nominative (marfūʿ).
﴿زنجبيلا﴾: the khabar of kāna, accusative (manṣūb).

muyesser-irab:18-18.t:
﴿عينا﴾: a badal (substitute) from ﴿زنجبيلا﴾ or from ﴿كأسا﴾, or accusative by way of specification (ikhtiṣāṣ).
﴿فيها﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿عينا﴾.
﴿تسمى﴾: an imperfect verb, passive (built for that whose agent is not named); the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "hiya" (it).
﴿سلسبيلا﴾: a second mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause ﴿تسمى﴾ is a second naʿt.

muyesser-irab:19-19.t:
﴿ويطوف﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «يطوف» is an imperfect verb.
﴿عليهم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يطوف﴾.
﴿ولدان﴾: fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ).
﴿مخلدون﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿ولدان﴾.
﴿إذا﴾: an adverb (ẓarf) for future time.
﴿رأيتهم﴾: a past verb; the tāʾ is the fāʿil and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause «رأيتهم» is in the position of a genitive, the adverb being put in construct with it.
﴿حسبتهم﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil and mafʿūl bihi.
﴿لؤلؤا﴾: a second mafʿūl bihi.
﴿منثورا﴾: naʿt.

muyesser-irab:20-20.t:
﴿وإذا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «إذا» is an adverb (ẓarf) for future time, containing the meaning of condition.
﴿رأيت﴾: a verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause «رأيت» is in the position of a genitive, the adverb being put in construct with it.
﴿ثم﴾: an adverb of place.
﴿رأيت﴾: a verb and its fāʿil; the clause «رأيت» has no grammatical position, because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition.
﴿نعيما﴾: the object of the second «رأيت».
﴿وملكا﴾: conjoined to ﴿نعيمًا﴾.
﴿كبيرا﴾: naʿt (adjective).

muyesser-irab:21-21.t:
﴿عاليهم﴾: an adverb of place (ẓarf makān), attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate).
﴿ثياب﴾: a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿سندس﴾: muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿خضر﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿ثياب﴾.
﴿وإستبرق﴾: conjoined to ﴿ثياب﴾ with the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "garments of إستبرق".
﴿وحلوا﴾: a past verb, passive (built for that whose agent is not named), and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is conjoined to ﴿ويطوف عليهم﴾.
﴿أساور﴾: a second mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and it was said: accusative by removal of the preposition.
﴿من فضة﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a naʿt of ﴿أساور﴾.
﴿وسقاهم﴾: a past verb and a fronted object, conjoined to «حلّوا».
﴿ربهم﴾: a postponed fāʿil (agent).
﴿شرابا﴾: a second mafʿūl bihi.
﴿طهورا﴾: a naʿt of ﴿شرابا﴾.

muyesser-irab:22-22.t:
﴿إن﴾: an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh); the clause is the content of an omitted saying (maqūl qawl maḥdhūf).
﴿هذا﴾: the noun of «إن», accusative (manṣūb).
﴿كان﴾: an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb; its noun is latent (mustatir).
﴿لكم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿جزاء﴾.
﴿جزاء﴾: the khabar of kāna; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of ﴿إن﴾.
﴿وكان﴾: a past verb; it is conjoined to the first ﴿كان﴾.
﴿سعيكم﴾: the noun of kāna.
﴿مشكورا﴾: the khabar of ﴿كان﴾.

muyesser-irab:23-23.t:
﴿إنا﴾: «إن» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and ﴿نا﴾ is its noun.
﴿نحن﴾: a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl), or a tawkīd (emphasis) of the noun of ﴿إن﴾.
﴿نزلنا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of «إنّ».
﴿عليك﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿نزلنا﴾.
﴿القرآن﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿تنزيلا﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).

muyesser-irab:24-24.t:
﴿فاصبر﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an implied condition), and «اصبر» is an imperative verb; its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "anta" (you).
﴿لحكم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿اصبر﴾.
﴿ربك﴾: muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿ولا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «لا» is prohibitive.
﴿تطع﴾: «تطع» is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by ﴿لا﴾; its fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "anta" (you).
﴿منهم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial).
﴿آثما﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿أو﴾: a conjunction.
﴿كفورا﴾: conjoined to ﴿آثما﴾.

muyesser-irab:25-25.t:
﴿واذكر﴾: an imperative verb; the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "anta" (you); the clause is conjoined to what came before.
﴿اسم﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿ربك﴾: muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿بكرة وأصيلا﴾: two adverbs (ẓarfs), attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿اذكر﴾.

muyesser-irab:26-26.t:
﴿ومن الليل﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿اسجد﴾.
﴿فاسجد﴾: an imperative verb; its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "anta" (you).
﴿له﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, also attached to ﴿اسجد﴾.
﴿وسبحه﴾: an imperative verb, its latent fāʿil, and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿ليلا﴾: an adverb (ẓarf), attached to ﴿سبحه﴾.
﴿طويلا﴾: naʿt (adjective).

muyesser-irab:27-27.t:
﴿إن﴾: an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh).
﴿هؤلاء﴾: the noun of «إن».
﴿يحبون﴾: an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent).
﴿العاجلة﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of «إن».
﴿ويذرون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «يذرون» is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.
﴿وراءهم﴾: an adverb of place (ẓarf makān), attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the object, placed before it.
﴿يوما﴾: mafʿūl bihi.
﴿ثقيلا﴾: naʿt (adjective).

muyesser-irab:28-28.t:
﴿نحن﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿خلقناهم﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the khabar (predicate).
﴿وشددنا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil.
﴿أسرهم﴾: mafʿūl bihi, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi.

muyesser-irab:29-29.t:
﴿إن﴾: an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh).
﴿هذه﴾: the noun of «إن».
﴿تذكرة﴾: the khabar (predicate) of «إن».
﴿فمن﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and «من» is conditional, mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿شاء﴾: a past verb in the position of a jussive (majzūm), the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ).
﴿اتخذ﴾: a past verb in the position of a jussive, the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ).
﴿إلى ربه﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted second mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿سبيلا﴾: the first object of «اتخذ».

muyesser-irab:30-30.t:
﴿وما﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «ما» is negating.
﴿تشاءون﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) is omitted.
﴿إلا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr).
﴿أن﴾: maṣdar-forming (maṣdariyya).
﴿يشاء﴾: an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb); the interpreted maṣdar is accusative as an adverb (ʿalā al-ẓarfiyya).
﴿الله﴾: fāʿil.
﴿إن﴾: an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh).
﴿الله﴾: the Name of Majesty, the noun of «إن».
﴿كان﴾: an abrogating (nāsikh) past verb.
﴿عليما حكيما﴾: two khabars of ﴿كان﴾; the clause «كان» is the khabar (predicate) of «إن».

muyesser-irab:31-31.t:
﴿يدخل﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); its fāʿil (agent) is "huwa" (He); and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause from «الله».
﴿من﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿يشاء﴾: an imperfect verb and a latent (mustatir) fāʿil; the clause ﴿يشاء﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿مَن﴾, with no grammatical position.
﴿في رحمته﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يدخل﴾.
﴿والظالمين﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «الظالمين» is accusative (manṣūb) by an implied (muqaddar) verb explained by what follows it.
﴿أعد﴾: a past verb and a latent fāʿil.
﴿لهم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أعدّ﴾.
﴿عذابا﴾: mafʿūl bihi.
﴿أليما﴾: naʿt (adjective).

nahhas-irab:1-2.t:
The first الإنسان, according to the exegetes, means Ādam, peace be upon him; and it may be that the genus is meant. The second is for the genus and nothing else. النطفة, in the usage of the Arabs, is a small amount of water in a vessel. أَمْشاجٍ is a naʿt (adjective) of نطفة, without any omission, according to the view of whoever says that الأمشاج are the veins that are in the نطفة — as you say: "man is limbs gathered together". Whoever says that الأمشاج are the fluid of the man and the fluid of the woman [also takes it] this way: He called the two together نطفة, and they mix and man is created from them. And whoever says:
الأمشاج are the clot and the lump of flesh — the construction in his view is "from a نطفة possessing أمشاج". The singular [of أمشاج] is مشيج, like شريف and أشراف; and one also says مشج, like عدل and أعدال. نَبْتَلِيهِ فَجَعَلْناهُ سَمِيعاً بَصِيراً: al-Farrāʾ said:
It is a case of fronting and postponement (taqdīm wa-taʾkhīr); in his view the meaning is: "We made man hearing and seeing in order to try him", i.e. to test him. Those who disagreed with him on this said: it is wrong on more than one count. One is that there is no fronting and postponement with the fāʾ, because it indicates that the second comes after the first. Another is that man is only tried — i.e. tested, commanded and forbidden — when he is of sound mind; he would be hearing and seeing [then], and was not so [before]. Another is that the context of the speech indicates something other than what he said, and there is no lām of kay in the speech; rather, the context of the speech is Allah, Mighty and Majestic, enumerating His blessings upon us and directing us to His blessings.

nahhas-irab:3-3.t: [شاكِراً and كَفُوراً are] both accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "We created man grateful or ungrateful". The meaning of إمّا is أو, even though it comes at the beginning of the speech to indicate the meaning. What shows you this is the statement of the exegetes that the meaning is: "We guided him to the way, either wretched or happy"; and wretchedness and happiness are decided «[Translator's note: the source has «بفرع منهما», apparently «يُفرغ منهما», "are settled".]» while he is in his mother's womb, and so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ informed. And it has been said: it is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara). Al-Farrāʾ permitted «ما» here to be redundant (zāʾida), and «إن» to be [the particle] of condition and requital, the meaning being: "We guided him to the way, whether he is grateful or ungrateful". Abū Jaʿfar said: this view is evidently wrong, because the «إن» of condition does not fall upon nouns, and the verse does not have إما شكر; it has إما شاكرا وإما كفورا, and these are two nouns, and nouns do not take the conditional construction according to any of the grammarians.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t: This is the reading of Abū ʿAmr and Ḥamza, without tanwīn [i.e. سَلاسِلَ]; except that what is sound from Ḥamza is that he used to pause on «سلاسلا» with alif, following the written text, because it is [written] with alif in the codices of the people of Medina and the people of Kufa. The reading of the people of Medina and the people of Kufa other than Ḥamza is «إنّا أعتدنا للكافرين سلاسلا وأغلالا وسعيرا». The argument for Abū ʿAmr and Ḥamza is that «سلاسل» is a diptote, because it is a plural with no counterpart among singulars; it is the ultimate plural pattern and so is heavy, and so is barred from tanwīn. And pausing on it with alif — the argument for it is that al-Ruʾāsī and al-Kisāʾī reported from the Arabs pausing on diptotes with alif, to make the fatḥa clear; so this reading is validated by the speech of the Arabs. The argument for those who gave it tanwīn is what al-Kisāʾī and other Kufans reported: that the Arabs make every diptote fully declinable, except أفعل منك. That is one argument. Another argument is that some theorists say: everything permissible in poetry is permissible in prose, because poetry is the foundation of the speech of the Arabs, so how can we dictate to their speech and treat poetry as outside it? A third argument is that since next to it there is a declinable plural, the first was made to follow the second.

nahhas-irab:5-5.t: The singular of الأبرار is برّ. Someone weak in Arabic sometimes errs and says: it is the plural of فعل likened to فعل «[Translator's note: the distinguishing vowels of these patterns (presumably فاعِل and فَعِل) have been lost in print.]» — and that is an error. It is the plural of فعل; one says بررت والدي, so I am بارّ and برّ; so برّ is [of the pattern] فعل, like حذرت فأنا حذر; and فعل / أفعال is a sound regular pattern. And it has been said: they were only called أبرار because they were dutiful (برّوا) to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, by obeying Him in performing His obligations and avoiding what He has forbidden. And it has been said: the meaning of كانَ مِزاجُها كافُوراً is [like camphor] in the fragrance of its scent.

nahhas-irab:6-6.t: عَيْناً: there is more than one way regarding its accusative. I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say: I heard Muḥammad ibn Yazīd say: I looked into its accusative, and nothing was sound for me in it except that it is accusative in the sense "I mean"; and likewise the second. That is one way. A second way is that it is in the sense of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in مزاجها. A fourth way «[Translator's note: so in the source; a third way is not mentioned.]» is that it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), the construction being: "they drink a spring, by which the servants of Allah drink, whose mixture is camphor". On يشرب بها there are two views. Al-Farrāʾ said: يشرب بها and يشربها are the same. Abū Jaʿfar said: better than this is that the meaning is "their thirst is quenched by it"; and I have mentioned it. يُفَجِّرُونَها تَفْجِيراً: [تَفْجِيراً is] a maṣdar (verbal noun). It is related that when one of them wants water to gush forth for him, he splits that place with a stick and water flows in it.

nahhas-irab:7-7.t:
يُوفُونَ بِالنَّذْرِ وَيَخافُونَ: and it [النذر] is everything a person is obliged to do, whether he vowed it or did not vow it. [Allah,] Mighty and Majestic, said: وَلْيُوفُوا نُذُورَهُمْ [al-Ḥajj: 29]. ʿAntara said: [al-Kāmil] 514-
الشّاتمي عرضي ولم أشتمهما ... والنّاذرين إذا لم القهما دمي
(The two who revile my honour though I have not reviled them, and who vowed my blood when I had not met them.)
Al-Farrāʾ's view: there is an implied «كان» in it, i.e. "they used to fulfil the vow in the world"; and likewise يَخافُونَ يَوْماً كانَ شَرُّهُ مُسْتَطِيراً.

nahhas-irab:8-8.t: The scholars differed about الأسير (the captive) here. Some of them said: he is from the people of war [i.e. non-Muslim enemies], because at that time there were no captives except from among them. Others said: it applies to the people of war and to the Muslims; and this is more appropriate given the generality of the verse, for it is not to be restricted except by decisive evidence; so it applies to those at that time and to those after, just as يُوفُونَ بِالنَّذْرِ does.

nahhas-irab:9-9.t: إِنَّما نُطْعِمُكُمْ لِوَجْهِ اللَّهِ, i.e. they say [this]. لا نريد منكم جزاء ولا شكورا: [شكورا] may be the plural of شكر, and it may be a maṣdar (verbal noun).

nahhas-irab:10-10.t:
Al-Farrāʾ said: القمطرير and القماطر mean "severe"; and he recited: [al-Ṭawīl] 515-
بني عمّنا هل تذكرون بلاءنا ... عليكم إذا ما كان يوم قماطر
(O sons of our uncle, do you remember our valour on your behalf, when there was a dire day?)

nahhas-irab:11-11.t: فَوَقاهُمُ اللَّهُ شَرَّ ذلِكَ الْيَوْمِ: [الْيَوْمِ is] a naʿt (adjective) of ذلك; and if you wish it is a badal (substitute). وَلَقَّاهُمْ نَضْرَةً وَسُرُوراً: al-Ḥasan said: radiance in the face, and joy in the heart.

nahhas-irab:12-12.t: Qatāda said: because they were patient in refraining from sins. This is the soundest view: one who refrains from sins is called صابر without qualification; and if you mean other than sins, you say صابر على كذا ("patient in such-and-such").

nahhas-irab:13-13.t: مُتَّكِئِينَ فِيها عَلَى الْأَرائِكِ: al-Farrāʾ said: مُتَّكِئِينَ is accusative by "cutting off" (qaṭʿ). According to the Basrans it is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the tāʾ and mīm [i.e. the pronoun هُمْ], and the governing word in it is جزى; and صبروا may not govern it, because مُتَّكِئِينَ is only in the Garden, while the patience was in this world. It may also be accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of جنة, and that is good because a pronoun refers back to it. لا يَرَوْنَ فِيها شَمْساً وَلا زَمْهَرِيراً: the view on it is like the view on «متكئين»; and its meaning is "not seeing" «[Translator's note: the source has «غير رائعين», apparently a misprint of «غير رائين».]».

nahhas-irab:14-15.t:
وَدانِيَةً عَلَيْهِمْ ظِلالُها: there are six ways in it. It may be conjoined to جَنَّةً, the adjective standing in place of the noun qualified, i.e. "and He rewarded them with a garden whose shade is close over them". It may be conjoined to متكئين. It may be conjoined to لا يرون, because its meaning is "not seeing". It may be accusative as praise, like وَالْمُقِيمِينَ الصَّلاةَ [al-Nisāʾ: 162] — even though it is indefinite, it resembles a definite. These are four ways. In the reading of Ibn Masʿūd: «ودانيا عليهم ظلالها», with the masculine of the plural; and in the reading of Ubayy: «ودان عليهم ظلالها». «دان» is in the position of rafʿ (nominative); its original form is داني; the vowel was found heavy on the yāʾ, so the ḍamma was dropped, and the yāʾ was dropped because it is vowelless and the tanwīn is vowelless. The vowel was not found heavy in ودانيا because of the lightness of the fatḥa. ظِلالُها is nominative by the [participle of] nearness, according to the view of those who put the first in the accusative; and whoever says «ودان ظلالها», in his view it [ظلالها] is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) and دان is its khabar (predicate), as you say مررت بزيد جالس أبوه, i.e. أبوه جالس. وَذُلِّلَتْ قُطُوفُها تَذْلِيلًا: a clause conjoined to a clause; therefore it was proper to bring the past tense although before it is an active participle. After it: وَيُطافُ عَلَيْهِمْ بِآنِيَةٍ مِنْ فِضَّةٍ وَأَكْوابٍ — the exegetes, among them Mujāhid, say: الكوب is the jug that has no handle; except Qatāda, who said: it is the cup. كانَتْ قَوارِيرَا: Abū ʿAmr's reading [has] the second without alif. He distinguished between them for two reasons: one is that it is so in the codices of the people of Basra; the second is that the first is at the end of a verse, so it is good to keep the alif in it.
As for Ḥamza, he read «كانت قوارير قوارير من فضّة» «[Translator's note: i.e. without tanwīn or alif in both.]», because they are both diptotes; this would be something clear were it not for its going against the written text. The Medinans read «[Translator's note: i.e. with tanwīn.]» in both of them; and what can be adduced in their favour is found only in the view of the Kufans, namely that al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ permitted making a diptote declinable, except أفعل منك; and al-Farrāʾ argued from the frequency of that in poetry.

nahhas-irab:16-16.t: قَدَّرُوها تَقْدِيراً: from al-Shaʿbī, Qatāda, Ibn Abzā and ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr, that they read قَدَّرُوها «[Translator's note: the source prints the standard vowels; their reading is the passive قُدِّرُوها.]», i.e. it was measured out for them, i.e. according to the measure of their Lord «[Translator's note: so in the source («على قدر ربّهم»); perhaps «ريّهم», "their thirst".]», neither exceeding that nor falling short.

nahhas-irab:17-17.t: وَيُسْقَوْنَ فِيها كَأْساً: Abū al-Ḥasan ibn Kaysān said: a cup is not called كأس until there is wine in it; likewise a table (خوان) is not called مائدة until there is food on it; and likewise الظعينة [is not so called until a woman is in the litter]. كانَ مِزاجُها زَنْجَبِيلًا, i.e. like ginger in its sting; they used to find that pleasant, so they were addressed according to what they knew.

nahhas-irab:18-18.t: عَيْناً: what has preceded suffices for discussing its accusative. تُسَمَّى سَلْسَبِيلًا: [سَلْسَبِيلًا is of the pattern] فعلليل, from السّلاسة (smoothness). Whoever says it is the name of the spring has made declinable what should not be declinable.

nahhas-irab:19-19.t: وَيَطُوفُ عَلَيْهِمْ وِلْدانٌ مُخَلَّدُونَ, i.e. with what they need. إِذا رَأَيْتَهُمْ حَسِبْتَهُمْ لُؤْلُؤاً مَنْثُوراً: the exegetes hold that the point of this simile is their great number and their beauty. ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar said: there is none of the people of the Garden but he has a thousand servant-boys, each boy at a task that his companion is not at.

nahhas-irab:20-20.t:
وَإِذا رَأَيْتَ ثَمَّ: the scholars of Arabic have three views on it. Most of the Basrans say: «ثمّ» is an adverb (ẓarf), and رأيت has not been made transitive, as you say ظننت في الدار, without making ظننت transitive, according to the view of Sībawayh. Al-Akhfash said — and it is one of the two views of al-Farrāʾ —: «ثمّ» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. "and when you look at there". Another view of al-Farrāʾ: he said the construction is "and when you see what is there", with «ما» dropped. Abū Jaʿfar said: «ثمّ», according to all the grammarians, is indeclinable (mabnī), not inflected, because of its shifting [reference]; and dropping «ما» is wrong according to the Basrans, because one would be dropping the relative noun and keeping the ṣila (relative clause), as if one brought part of a noun. رَأَيْتَ نَعِيماً وَمُلْكاً كَبِيراً is the apodosis (jawāb) of «إذا». What makes clear to you the meaning of this is what Aḥmad ibn ʿAlī ibn Sahl narrated to us; he said: Zuhayr — meaning Ibn Ḥarb — narrated to us: Muḥammad ibn Ḥāzim narrated to us: ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Abjar narrated to us, from Thuwayr ibn Abī Fākhita, from Ibn ʿUmar, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said:
"The lowest of the people of the Garden in rank will look over his kingdom for two thousand years, looking at his spouses, his couches and his servants; and the highest of them in rank will look at the face of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, twice every day." ]

nahhas-irab:21-21.t:
عالِيَهُمْ ثِيابُ سُندُسٍ «[Translator's note: the source prints عالِيَهُمْ with fatḥa although it describes the nominative reading عالِيْهِمْ; likewise the vowelling of several readings below has been lost in print.]»: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); the original is عاليُهم, the ḍamma being dropped because of its heaviness. This is a clear reading, and it is the reading of Abū Jaʿfar, Nāfiʿ, Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, al-Aʿmash and Ḥamza. Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, al-Ḥasan, Abū ʿAmr, al-Kisāʾī, Ibn Kathīr and ʿĀṣim read عالِيَهُمْ in the accusative as an adverb (ẓarf); and al-Farrāʾ compared it to his saying زيد داخل الدار. Abū Jaʿfar said: as for عاليهم, it is clear that it is accusative as an adverb. There are two views on its meaning: one is that the green covers the garments of the people of the Garden; the other is that this green growth is above their canopies, not on them. As for زيد داخل الدار, it is not permissible according to a group of grammarians, just as one does not say زيد الدار; but if you said زيد خارج الدار it would be permissible. ʿAbd al-Wārith related from Ḥumayd from Mujāhid that he read «عليهم ثياب سندس». Abū Jaʿfar said: this needs no explanation. In the reading of Ibn Masʿūd: «عاليتهم ثياب سندس», with the feminine of the group. Al-Ḥasan and Nāfiʿ read «ثياب سندس خضر وإستبرق» «[Translator's note: i.e. both nominative.]»; al-Aʿmash and Ḥamza read «ثياب سندس خضر وإستبرق» with both in the genitive; Abū ʿAmr and Abū Jaʿfar read «ثياب سندس خضر وإستبرق» with «خضر» nominative and «إستبرق» genitive; and Ibn Kathīr and ʿĀṣim read «ثياب سندس خضر وإستبرق» «[Translator's note: i.e. with خضر genitive and إستبرق nominative.]». Ibn Muḥayṣin read «وإستبرق» with a connecting alif and without tanwīn. Abū Jaʿfar said: the first reading is good, the nominative running continuously throughout: خضر is a naʿt (adjective) of the garments and إستبرق is conjoined to them;
it is declinable because it is indefinite, and the alif was made disjunctive (hamzat qaṭʿ) because it is a noun; if you named a man استكبر, you would say:
جاءني استكبر [with disjunctive hamza]. This is the view of al-Khalīl and Sībawayh. The second reading is on the basis that whoever reads it qualifies سندس with خضر. There is some remoteness in that, because one only says هذا سندس أخضر, as one says هذا حرير أخضر; but that is permissible because it is a genus, and a genus expresses a plurality, as in your saying: سندس and سندسات are the same; and he conjoined وإستبرق to سندس, i.e. "and garments of إستبرق". The third reading is also good: he made خُضْرٌ a naʿt of the garments — and that is the clear, good way — and put إستبرق in the genitive, also conjoined to سندس. In the fourth reading, خضر is genitive as a naʿt of سندس, as has passed, and وإستبرق is nominative because it is conjoined to ثياب. The reading of Ibn Muḥayṣin is, according to everyone we know among the scholars of Arabic who mentioned the readings, a solecism, because he made إستبرق a diptote although it is indefinite. His making it a diptote cannot be except for one of two reasons: either he made it a diptote because it is foreign, or because it is on the pattern of a verb; and the foreign noun and what is on the pattern of a verb are both declinable when indefinite. Moreover, he made the alif connective, and that is wrong according to al-Khalīl and Sībawayh, for the reason we mentioned. And he put «إستبرق» in the accusative — even if one could contrive [a justification] for its accusative — so this is what is in it, part of which has been mentioned. Abū Jaʿfar said: if one were to contrive [a justification] for it, saying that it is a past verb, i.e. "and this collection gleamed" «[Translator's note: i.e. إستبرق read as the verb اسْتَبْرَقَ.]», that would in my view be something permissible, though I do not know of anyone who has mentioned it. وَحُلُّوا أَساوِرَ مِنْ فِضَّةٍ: some heretics have attacked this, either out of ignorance of the language or intending unbelief, in audacity against Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and to gain some of the debris of this world. That is because the Garden has no buying or selling, so there is no sense in his attack on the grounds of the low value of silver. And [as for the claim] that this does not befit men — he is ignorant of the meaning of the exegesis, because in the exegesis it is that this will be for their wives; and even if it were for them, that would not detract from its beauty. He also attacked الإستبرق, either not knowing its meaning, or knowing it «[Translator's note: «داره» in the source, apparently «دراه».]» and deliberately intending unbelief. الإستبرق, according to «[Translator's note: the source has «عنه», apparently «عند».]» the Arabs, is what is strong and thick in itself, not thick in its threads.
Abū Jaʿfar said: we have mentioned that this إستبرق will be above their canopies. وَسَقاهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ شَراباً طَهُوراً, i.e. pure of filth, impurities and dirt.

nahhas-irab:22-22.t: إِنَّ هذا كانَ لَكُمْ جَزاءً: it is permissible to put جزاء in the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of «إنّ», with «كان» then cancelled [i.e. non-governing]. وَكانَ سَعْيُكُمْ مَشْكُوراً: [مَشْكُوراً is] the khabar of «كان»; and if it were nominative, it would be permissible for the noun of كان to be implied in it [i.e. the pronoun of the matter]; and it is not cancelled «[Translator's note: «تغلى» in the source, a misprint of «تلغى».]» when it begins [the clause], because the speech is built on it.

nahhas-irab:23-23.t: إِنَّا نَحْنُ نَزَّلْنا عَلَيْكَ الْقُرْآنَ: «نحن» may be in the position of naṣb (accusative) as an adjective [i.e. tawkīd (emphasis)] of the noun of إنّ; it may be a separating pronoun (fāṣila) with no position; and it may be in the position of rafʿ (nominative) as a mubtadaʾ (subject), with the khabar (predicate) being «نزّلنا». تَنْزِيلًا is a maṣdar (verbal noun) brought for emphasis.

nahhas-irab:24-24.t: فَاصْبِرْ لِحُكْمِ رَبِّكَ, i.e. be patient with their harm. The occasion for the revelation of this, according to what Qatāda mentioned, was that Abū Jahl said: "If I see Muḥammad ﷺ, I will tread on his neck." وَلا تُطِعْ مِنْهُمْ آثِماً أَوْ كَفُوراً: al-Farrāʾ said: «أو» has the status of «لا», i.e. "do not obey one who sins, nor one who disbelieves". Abū Jaʿfar said: «أو», in interrogation, conditional requital and negation, has the status of «لا». Abū Jaʿfar said: and the meaning may be "do not obey one who sins and disbelieves in any way", so that it is close in meaning to the wāw. Abū Jaʿfar said: the first view is correct according to the view of Sībawayh, and the second is wrong: «أو» does not mean the wāw, because when you say لا تكلّم زيدا أو عمرا, its meaning is "do not speak to either one of them, nor to both of them if they are together". The wāw is not like that: when you say [it with the wāw], the one commanded, if he speaks to one of them, is not disobeying his command; but with «أو», if he speaks to one of them, he is disobeying his command. Likewise in the verse: neither the sinner nor the ungrateful may be obeyed.

nahhas-irab:25-25.t: بُكْرَةً may be definite, and then it is a diptote, or indefinite, and then it is declinable. Here it is indefinite, which is why it has tanwīn, because after it comes وَأَصِيلًا, which is indefinite; and it is not definite unless the alif and lām enter it.

nahhas-irab:26-26.t: وَمِنَ اللَّيْلِ فَاسْجُدْ لَهُ: the construction is "so prostrate to Him in part of the night". وَسَبِّحْهُ لَيْلًا طَوِيلًا: it has been said: it is abrogated by the removal of the obligation of the night prayer; it has been said: it is by way of recommendation; and it has been said: it is specific to the Prophet ﷺ.

nahhas-irab:27-27.t:
إِنَّ هؤُلاءِ يُحِبُّونَ الْعاجِلَةَ, i.e. they love the good of this world. وَيَذَرُونَ وَراءَهُمْ يَوْماً ثَقِيلًا: Sufyān said: it means the Hereafter. Abū Jaʿfar said: it has been said that وراء means "in front"; and even those who reject [the existence of] words with opposite meanings (aḍdād) allow this, because وراء is derived from توارى ("to be concealed"), so it applies to what is in front of you and what is behind you. And it has been said:
The construction is: "and they leave behind them [the] work [for] a heavy day", i.e. they do not work for the Hereafter.

nahhas-irab:28-28.t:
نَحْنُ خَلَقْناهُمْ وَشَدَدْنا أَسْرَهُمْ: from Abū Hurayra, who said: [it means] the joints. Ibn Zayd said:
Strength. And it has been said: it is the place of excretion «[Translator's note: «الحديث» in the source, apparently a misprint of «الحَدَث».]». Among the best of what has been said about it is the view of Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid and Qatāda; they said: أسرهم means their constitution. Abū Jaʿfar said: it would be from their saying ما أحسن أسر هذا الرجل, i.e. his build; and from this is أخذه بأسره, i.e. in his entirety and his whole frame, leaving nothing of him. وَإِذا شِئْنا بَدَّلْنا أَمْثالَهُمْ تَبْدِيلًا: Ibn Zayd said: it means the children of Ādam who opposed obedience to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and their likes are also from the children of Ādam.

nahhas-irab:29-29.t: إِنَّ هذِهِ تَذْكِرَةٌ: it has been said: i.e. these parables and stories. فَمَنْ شاءَ اتَّخَذَ إِلى رَبِّهِ سَبِيلًا, i.e. whoever wills takes a path to the pleasure of his Lord, through obedience to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and abstaining from disobeying Him.

nahhas-irab:30-30.t:
وَما تَشاؤُنَ taking the way, except by Allah willing that, because the will is His. The bāʾ was dropped, so «أن» came to be in the position of naṣb (accusative); and some grammarians say: it is in the position of khafḍ (genitive).
إِنَّ اللَّهَ كانَ عَلِيماً, i.e. of whoever He wills to take a path to His pleasure; حَكِيماً in His management, no one being able to escape from it.

nahhas-irab:31-31.t:
يُدْخِلُ مَنْ يَشاءُ فِي رَحْمَتِهِ, i.e. by granting him success in repentance, so he repents and enters the Garden. وَالظَّالِمِينَ أَعَدَّ لَهُمْ عَذاباً أَلِيماً: according to Sībawayh, الظالمين is accusative by an implied verb explained by what follows, i.e. "and He punishes the wrongdoers". As for the Kufans, they said: it was put in the accusative because the wāw is a ẓarf (container) for the verb, i.e. a container for أعدّ. Abū Jaʿfar said: this needs to make clear what the governing word of the accusative is. Al-Farrāʾ added to the difficulty in this by saying:
Its nominative is permissible, and it is like وَالشُّعَراءُ يَتَّبِعُهُمُ الْغاوُونَ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 224]. Abū Jaʿfar said:
This does not resemble that in any way, except remotely, because before this there is a verb, so the accusative was chosen in it, so as to imply a governing verb, and thus conjoin what a verb governs to what a verb governs; whereas الشعراء is not preceded by a verb — it is preceded only by a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate). [Allah,] Mighty and Majestic, said:
وَأَكْثَرُهُمْ كاذِبُونَ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 223]; while here [before it] is يدخل من يشاء في رحمته. The nominative is permissible on the basis of cutting it off from the first. Abū Ḥātim said: al-Aṣmaʿī narrated to me; he said: I heard someone read:
«والظّالمون أعدّ لهم عذابا أليما» in the nominative; and in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: «وللظّالمين أعدّ لهم عذابا أليما», with the lām repeated.

safi-cedvel:1-1.t:
* I'rab:
(هل) an interrogative particle for affirmation (al-taqrīr) [Note: Or meaning قد.]; (على الإنسان) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أتى); (حين) fāʿil (agent) of أتى, nominative.
The clause «أتى ... حين» has no grammatical position: an opening clause (ibtidāʾiyya).
The clause «لم يكن ...» is in the position of an accusative: ḥāl (circumstantial) of الإنسان [Note: Or in the position of a nominative as naʿt (adjective) of حين, with the linking pronoun implied in it.].

* Morphology:
(حين): a noun meaning an indefinite period, long or short; its pattern is فعل, with kasra then sukūn.
(الدهر): a noun for extended, unlimited time; its pattern is فعل, with fatḥa then sukūn.
(مذكور): passive participle of the triliteral ذكر; its pattern is مفعول.

safi-cedvel:2-2.t:
* I'rab:
(من نطفة) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (خلقنا); (أمشاج) naʿt (adjective) of (نطفة) [Note: The adjective comes in the plural because النطفة has a plural sense, or because every part of the drop is a drop.], genitive; (الفاء) conjunction; (سميعا) ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, of the object, by making the verb carry the meaning of خلقناه; (بصيرا) a second ḥāl, accusative..
The clause «إنّا خلقنا ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «خلقنا ...» is in the position of a nominative: khabar (predicate) of إنّ.
The clause «نبتليه ...» is in the position of an accusative: ḥāl of the fāʿil (agent) of خلقنا or of the object [Note: The clause may be resumptive, and so have no grammatical position.].
The clause «جعلناه ...» is in the position of a nominative: conjoined to the clause خلقنا..

* Morphology:
(أمشاج): plural of مشج, on the pattern فعل with two fatḥas, or with fatḥa then sukūn, meaning a mixture.

safi-cedvel:3-3.t:
* I'rab:
(إمّا) a particle for detailing the states; (شاكرا) ḥāl (circumstantial) of the object of هديناه, accusative; (الواو) conjunction..
The clause «إنّا هديناه ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «هديناه ...» is in the position of a nominative: khabar (predicate) of إنّ.

* Rhetoric:
In the saying of Allah the Exalted «إِنَّا هَدَيْناهُ السَّبِيلَ إِمَّا شاكِراً وَإِمَّا كَفُوراً ...».
Since those characterized by gratitude are few, He said «شاكرا ...», expressing it with the active participle to indicate its scarcity. As for bringing كفور in the intensive form, it is for the sake of the verse-endings, and to signal that man is seldom free of some ingratitude, so those characterized by it are many, and it occurs often from man.

* Benefits:
- (إمّا):
It is a particle of condition and detailing, and it has five meanings:
1- Doubt, as in: (جاءني إما حسن وإما حسين) "either Ḥasan or Ḥusayn came to me", when you do not know which of the two came.
1- Doubt, as in: (جاءني إما حسن وإما حسين), when you do not know which of the two came. [Translator's note: this item is printed twice in the source.]
2- Vagueness (al-ibhām), as in the saying of the Exalted: «وَآخَرُونَ مُرْجَوْنَ لِأَمْرِ اللَّهِ إِمَّا يُعَذِّبُهُمْ وَإِمَّا يَتُوبُ عَلَيْهِمْ ...».
3- Choice (al-takhyīr), as in the saying of the Exalted (إِمَّا أَنْ تُلْقِيَ وَإِمَّا أَنْ نَكُونَ أَوَّلَ مَنْ أَلْقى).
4- Permission (al-ibāḥa), as in (جالس إما الحسن وإما ابن سيرين) "sit with either al-Ḥasan or Ibn Sīrīn". 5- Detailing (al-tafṣīl), as in the saying of the Exalted: (إِنَّا هَدَيْناهُ السَّبِيلَ إِمَّا شاكِراً وَإِمَّا كَفُوراً).
With (إما), the speech is built — from the very beginning — on what it was brought for, whether doubt or something else; therefore it must be repeated, except rarely. With (أو), the speech opens on certainty, and then doubt or something else supervenes; and for this reason it is not repeated.

safi-cedvel:4-4.t:
* I'rab:
(للكافرين) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أعتدنا); and (سلاسل) is denied tanwīn because it is a plural on the pattern of the furthest plurals (ṣīghat muntahā al-jumūʿ).
The clause «إنّا أعتدنا ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «أعتدنا ...» is in the position of a nominative: khabar (predicate) of إنّ.

safi-cedvel:5-10.t:
* I'rab:
(من كأس) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يشربون); (عينا) badal (substitute) of (كافورا), accusative [Note: Or a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) whose governor is the preceding يشربون, with the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "the water of a spring".. or it is the mafʿūl bihi of an omitted verb by way of ishtighāl (preoccupation), likewise with the omission of a muḍāf, and the clause after it is explicative.]; (بها) attached to (يشرب), by making it carry the meaning of يلتذّ "delights" or يرتوي "quenches his thirst" [Note: Or without that implication, if the pronoun refers to الكأس.. or it is attached to a ḥāl of عينا if it is a proper name in itself.. Some exegetes made the bāʾ redundant, i.e. يشربها, taking as evidence one of the readings in which the verb takes the pronoun directly.]; (تفجيرا) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative.
The clause «إنّ الأبرار يشربون ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يشربون ...» is in the position of a nominative: khabar (predicate) of إنّ.
The clause «كان مزاجها كافورا ...» is in the position of a genitive: naʿt (adjective) of كأس.
The clause «يشرب بها ...» is in the position of an accusative: naʿt of عينا [Note: If the pronoun in (بها) refers to الكأس, the clause is a second naʿt of الكأس, in the position of a genitive.]. The clause «يفجّرونها ...» is in the position of an accusative: ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of يشرب.
7- (بالنذر) attached to (يوفون); (يوما) mafʿūl bihi, accusative..
The clause «يوفون ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) — or giving the reason for what preceded —. The clause «يخافون ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause يوفون.
The clause «كان شرّه مستطيرا ...» is in the position of an accusative: naʿt of (يوما).
8- (الواو) conjunction; (على حبّه) a ḥāl of the fāʿil or of the object..
The clause «يطعمون ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause يوفون.
9- (إنّما) the restraining particle and the restrained (kāffa wa-makfūfa); (لوجه) attached to a ḥāl of the fāʿil of نطعم [Note: Or attached to (نطعمكم), and the lām is causal.]; (لا) negative; (منكم) attached to (نريد); the second (لا) is redundant (zāʾida), to emphasize the negation; (شكورا) conjoined to (جزاء), accusative like it.
The clause «نطعمكم ...» is in the position of an accusative: the object of speech of an implied verb of saying, which is a ḥāl of the fāʿil of يطعمون, i.e. "they give food, saying: we feed you only ...".
The clause «لا نريد ...» is in the position of an accusative: ḥāl of the fāʿil of نطعمكم.
10- (من ربّنا) attached to (نخاف) [Note: Or attached to a ḥāl of (يوما) — an adjective that has come before the noun it qualifies —]..
